observations.title: sdd/auth-rbac/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: Auth & RBAC System for CRM

### Current State
El proyecto Startup CRM no tiene sistema de autenticación ni control de acceso implementado. Es un sistema nuevo que requiere autenticación robusta multi-usuario con permisos granulares.

### Affected Areas
- backend/ — Donde se implementarán los endpoints de auth y middleware de RBAC
- frontend/ — Donde se implementarán las páginas de login, register, y gestión de usuarios
- Base de datos PostgreSQL — Nuevas tablas para usuarios, roles, permisos, workspaces

### Approaches

1. **Enfoque Monolítico con JWT** — Implementar auth directamente en el backend Node.js con JWT
   - Pros: Simple, rápido de implementar, sin dependencias externas
   - Cons: Mantenimiento de tokens, refresh manual
   - Effort: Medium

2. **Enfoque con OAuth + JWT** — Usar Google OAuth 2.0 como proveedor principal + JWT interno
   - Pros: Seguridad reforzada, login social很简单, menos riesgo de password handling
   - Cons: Dependencia de Google, requiere más configuración
   - Effort: Medium-High

3. **Enfoque Microservicio de Auth** — Crear un microservicio dedicado para auth
   - Pros: Aislamiento, escalabilidad, reusabilidad
   - Cons: Complejidad operacional, más servicios para mantener
   - Effort: High

### Recommendation
**Enfoque 2: OAuth + JWT** con las siguientes razones:
- El usuario específicamente pidió Google OAuth 2.0
- JWT con refresh rotation es estándar de la industria
- El equipo de 8 personas puede mantener un sistema centralizado sin sobreingeniería
- Multi-tenancy con workspaces es un requisito del negocio

### Riesgos
- Gestión de sesiones expiradas puede ser compleja
- Sincronización de permisos entre workspaces requiere diseño cuidadoso
- Google OAuth puede fallar si hay problemas de red/API

### Ready for Proposal
Yes — La exploración está lista para crear la propuesta formal del sistema de auth.

observations.title: sdd/auth-rbac/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Auth & RBAC System

## Intent

Implementar un sistema completo de autenticación y control de acceso basado en roles (RBAC) para el CRM, permitiendo login con email/password y Google OAuth 2.0, con soporte multi-tenant mediante workspaces.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Sistema de autenticación con JWT y refresh token rotation
- Login con email/password (registro, login, logout)
- Login con Google OAuth 2.0
- Sistema de roles: Admin, Manager, Sales, Support, Viewer
- Permisos granulares por módulo (leer, crear, editar, eliminar)
- Gestión de usuarios (Admin puede crear/editar/eliminar usuarios)
- Multi-tenancy con workspaces aislamientods de datos
- Middleware de protección para endpoints

### Out of Scope
- Autenticación con otros proveedores OAuth (Facebook, GitHub, etc.)
- SSO empresarial (SAML)
- 2FA/MFA avanzado
- Login con redes sociales adicionales
- Historial de auditoría de acciones de usuarios

## Approach

Implementar un sistema centralizado de auth en el backend Node.js con:
- JWT para access tokens (15 min) + refresh tokens (7 días) con rotation
- Google OAuth 2.0 integrado con Passport.js o similar
- RBAC basado en middleware con permisos por recurso/acción
- PostgreSQL con tablas para users, roles, permissions, workspaces
- Workspace middleware que filtra datos por organización

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `backend/src/auth/` | New | Módulos de autenticación y RBAC |
| `backend/src/middleware/` | New | Auth middleware y workspace isolation |
| `backend/src/database/migrations/` | New | Tablas de auth y workspaces |
| `frontend/src/pages/auth/` | New | Páginas de login, register |
| `frontend/src/contexts/` | New | Auth context para estado global |
| `frontend/src/components/` | New | Componentes protegidos, UI de gestión |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Refresh token theft | Low | Rotation de tokens, storage seguro (httpOnly cookie) |
| Google OAuth failure | Low | Fallback a email/password, manejo de errores |
| Workspace data leak | Medium | Middleware de aislamiento obligatorio en cada query |
| Session hijacking | Low | JWT con expiración corta, IP validation opcional |

## Rollback Plan

1. Revertir migraciones de base de datos
2. Eliminar directorios auth/, middleware/ del backend
3. Eliminar páginas y componentes de auth del frontend
4. Deshabilitar rutas protegidas en el router

## Dependencies

- PostgreSQL existente
- Google Cloud Console project con OAuth credentials
- Backend Node.js con Express o framework similar
- Frontend Next.js

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Usuario puede registrarse con email/password
- [ ] Usuario puede hacer login con email/password
- [ ] Usuario puede hacer login con Google OAuth
- [ ] Access token expira en 15 min, refresh en 7 días
- [ ] Refresh rotation funciona correctamente
- [ ] Logout invalida refresh token
- [ ] 5 roles definidos con permisos específicos
- [ ] Admin puede gestionar usuarios (CRUD)
- [ ] Datos filtrados por workspace del usuario
- [ ] Endpoints protegidos rechazan requests sin token válido

observations.title: sdd/auth-rbac/spec
observations.content:
# Auth & RBAC Specification

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: User Registration

The system MUST allow users to register with email and password. The password MUST be hashed using bcrypt with minimum 10 rounds. The system MUST create a default workspace for the user upon registration.

#### Scenario: Successful registration with email/password

- GIVEN the user provides a valid email and password (min 8 chars)
- WHEN the user submits the registration form
- THEN the system creates a new user record with hashed password
- AND creates a default workspace owned by the user
- AND returns a success response with user data

#### Scenario: Registration with duplicate email

- GIVEN a user with email "test@example.com" already exists
- WHEN a new user attempts to register with the same email
- THEN the system returns a 409 Conflict error
- AND displays "Email already registered" message

### Requirement: User Login with Email/Password

The system MUST authenticate users with email and password credentials. The system MUST issue a JWT access token and a refresh token upon successful authentication.

#### Scenario: Successful login with email/password

- GIVEN a registered user with email "test@example.com" and password "validPassword123"
- WHEN the user submits valid credentials
- THEN the system validates the password against the hash
- AND returns a 200 OK with access token (15 min expiry) and refresh token (7 days expiry)

#### Scenario: Login with invalid password

- GIVEN a registered user exists with password "correctPassword"
- WHEN the user submits the correct email but wrong password
- THEN the system returns 401 Unauthorized
- AND displays "Invalid credentials" message

#### Scenario: Login with non-existent email

- GIVEN no user exists with email "nonexistent@example.com"
- WHEN a user attempts to login with that email
- THEN the system returns 401 Unauthorized
- AND displays "Invalid credentials" message

### Requirement: Google OAuth 2.0 Login

The system MUST allow users to authenticate using their Google account via OAuth 2.0. If the Google email doesn't exist in the system, it MUST create a new user automatically.

#### Scenario: Login with existing Google account

- GIVEN a user previously registered via Google OAuth with email "user@gmail.com"
- WHEN the user initiates Google OAuth flow and authorizes the app
- THEN the system finds the existing user by Google ID
- AND returns access token and refresh token

#### Scenario: First-time Google OAuth login

- GIVEN no user exists with Google email "newuser@gmail.com"
- WHEN the user initiates Google OAuth and authorizes the app
- THEN the system creates a new user with Google provider
- AND creates a default workspace for the user
- AND returns access token and refresh token

### Requirement: JWT Token Management

The system MUST issue JSON Web Tokens for session management. Access tokens MUST expire after 15 minutes. Refresh tokens MUST be rotated on each use and expire after 7 days.

#### Scenario: Access token refresh

- GIVEN a user has a valid refresh token
- WHEN the user requests a new access token using the refresh token
- THEN the system validates the refresh token
- AND issues a new access token
- AND rotates the refresh token (issues new one, invalidates old)

#### Scenario: Expired access token

- GIVEN a user's access token has expired
- WHEN the user makes an API request with the expired token
- THEN the system returns 401 Unauthorized
- AND the client should use the refresh token to get a new access token

#### Scenario: Invalid or revoked refresh token

- GIVEN a user's refresh token has been revoked (logout or theft)
- WHEN the user attempts to refresh the access token
- THEN the system returns 401 Unauthorized
- AND the user must re-authenticate

### Requirement: User Logout

The system MUST allow users to logout, invalidating their refresh token.

#### Scenario: Successful logout

- GIVEN an authenticated user with an active refresh token
- WHEN the user calls the logout endpoint
- THEN the system marks the refresh token as revoked
- AND returns 200 OK

### Requirement: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

The system MUST define five roles: Admin, Manager, Sales, Support, and Viewer. Each role MUST have specific permissions per module. The system MUST enforce these permissions on all protected endpoints.

#### Roles Matrix

| Role    | Users | Contacts | Deals | Tasks | Reports | Settings |
|---------|-------|----------|-------|-------|---------|----------|
| Admin   | CRUD  | CRUD     | CRUD  | CRUD  | CRUD    | CRUD     |
| Manager | CRUD  | CRUD     | CRUD  | CRUD  | Read    | Read     |
| Sales   | Read  | CRU      | CRU   | CRU   | Read    | None     |
| Support | Read  | Read     | Read  | CRU   | None    | None     |
| Viewer  | Read  | Read     | Read  | Read  | Read    | None     |

#### Scenario: Admin accesses user management

- GIVEN a user with Admin role
- WHEN the user requests to list all users
- THEN the system returns the user list
- AND allows user creation, editing, and deletion

#### Scenario: Viewer tries to create a contact

- GIVEN a user with Viewer role
- WHEN the user attempts to create a new contact
- THEN the system returns 403 Forbidden
- AND displays "Insufficient permissions" message

### Requirement: User Management by Admin

The system MUST allow Admin users to create, read, update, and delete user accounts within their workspace.

#### Scenario: Admin creates a new user

- GIVEN an authenticated Admin user
- WHEN the Admin creates a new user with email, name, and role
- THEN the system creates the user in the Admin's workspace
- AND sends an invitation email (or displays temp password)

#### Scenario: Admin deletes a user

- GIVEN an authenticated Admin user
- WHEN the Admin deletes another user from the workspace
- THEN the system soft-deletes the user
- AND revokes all their active tokens

### Requirement: Multi-Tenant Workspace Isolation

The system MUST isolate data by workspace. Users MUST only access data belonging to their workspace.

#### Scenario: User accesses other workspace data

- GIVEN a user belongs to Workspace A
- WHEN the user requests data from Workspace B
- THEN the system returns 403 Forbidden
- AND logs the unauthorized access attempt

#### Scenario: Workspace transfer

- GIVEN an Admin user
- WHEN the Admin transfers a user to another workspace
- THEN the system updates the user's workspace_id
- AND the user loses access to the old workspace data

## MODIFIED Requirements

None - this is a new feature.

## REMOVED Requirements

None.

observations.title: sdd/auth-rbac/design
observations.content:
# Design: Auth & RBAC System

## Technical Approach

El sistema de auth será implementado como módulos centralizados en el backend Node.js, utilizando JWT con refresh token rotation. El frontend Next.js consumirá los endpoints y mantendrá el estado de autenticación via React Context. La base de datos PostgreSQL almacenará usuarios, roles, permisos y workspaces.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: JWT + Refresh Token Rotation

**Choice**: Access tokens JWT (15 min) + Refresh tokens con rotación en DB
**Alternatives considered**: Tokens simples sin rotación, Session-based, OAuth-only
**Rationale**: Balance entre seguridad (expiración corta) y UX (no pedir login cada 15 min). Refresh rotation mitiga el riesgo de token robado.

### Decision: Roles y Permisos en Base de Datos

**Choice**: Roles y permisos almacenados en PostgreSQL, verificados en middleware
**Alternatives considered**: Hardcoded en código, JWT claims
**Rationale**: Flexibilidad para modificar permisos sin deploy. Admin puede gestionar desde la UI.

### Decision: Workspace Isolation via Middleware

**Choice**: Middleware obligatorio que añade workspace_id a todas las queries
**Alternatives considered**: Filter en cada query manualmente, Row-level security
**Rationale**: Middleware es más mantenible y menos propenso a errores. Row-level security es buena opción futura.

### Decision: Google OAuth con Passport.js

**Choice**: Passport.js con Google Strategy para OAuth
**Alternatives considered**: Implementación manual de OAuth flow
**Rationale**: Passport es estándar de la industria, bien mantenido, fácil de integrar.

## Data Flow

```
┌─────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│   Frontend  │────▶│  API Gateway │────▶│  Auth Service  │
│  (Next.js)  │◀────│   (Express)  │◀────│  (Middleware)   │
└─────────────┘     └──────────────┘     └─────────────────┘
                           │                      │
                           ▼                      ▼
                    ┌──────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
                    │   PostgreSQL │◀────│  JWT Validator  │
                    └──────────────┘     └─────────────────┘
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `backend/src/auth/` | Create | Módulos: jwt.service.ts, oauth.service.ts, auth.controller.ts |
| `backend/src/auth/strategies/` | Create | Passport strategies: local.strategy.ts, google.strategy.ts |
| `backend/src/auth/decorators/` | Create | Decoradores: @CurrentUser, @Roles, @Permissions |
| `backend/src/middleware/auth.middleware.ts` | Create | Valida JWT, attach user al request |
| `backend/src/middleware/workspace.middleware.ts` | Create | Filtra queries por workspace_id |
| `backend/src/middleware/rbac.middleware.ts` | Create | Verifica permisos del rol |
| `backend/src/database/migrations/` | Create | Tablas: users, roles, permissions, user_roles, workspaces, refresh_tokens |
| `backend/src/entities/` | Create | TypeORM entities o Prisma schemas |
| `frontend/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx` | Create | Estado global de autenticación |
| `frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.ts` | Create | Hook para acceder al contexto |
| `frontend/src/hooks/usePermission.ts` | Create | Hook para verificar permisos |
| `frontend/src/pages/auth/login.tsx` | Create | Página de login |
| `frontend/src/pages/auth/register.tsx` | Create | Página de registro |
| `frontend/src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx` | Create | Wrapper para rutas protegidas |
| `frontend/src/components/RoleGuard.tsx` | Create | Componente para verificar roles |

## Database Schema

```sql
-- workspaces (multi-tenant)
CREATE TABLE workspaces (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- users
CREATE TABLE users (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  password_hash VARCHAR(255),  -- null si OAuth
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  workspace_id UUID REFERENCES workspaces(id),
  google_id VARCHAR(255),       -- null si no es OAuth
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- roles
CREATE TABLE roles (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL  -- admin, manager, sales, support, viewer
);

-- permissions
CREATE TABLE permissions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  resource VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,    -- users, contacts, deals, tasks
  action VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,        -- create, read, update, delete
  role_id UUID REFERENCES roles(id)
);

-- refresh_tokens
CREATE TABLE refresh_tokens (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  token VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  expires_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  revoked BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

## Interfaces / Contracts

### Auth Endpoints

```
POST /auth/register
  Body: { email, password, name }
  Response: { user, accessToken, refreshToken }

POST /auth/login
  Body: { email, password }
  Response: { accessToken, refreshToken }

POST /auth/google
  Body: { googleToken: string }
  Response: { accessToken, refreshToken }

POST /auth/refresh
  Body: { refreshToken }
  Response: { accessToken, refreshToken }

POST /auth/logout
  Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
  Body: { refreshToken }
  Response: { success: true }
```

### Protected Endpoints Pattern

```
GET /api/users
  Headers: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
  Response: { users: User[] }
  Requires: role=admin OR permission=users:read

POST /api/users
  Headers: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
  Body: { email, name, roleId }
  Requires: role=admin OR permission=users:create
```

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Unit | JWT generation/validation, password hashing, permission checks | Jest + mocks |
| Integration | Auth flow completo, refresh rotation, workspace isolation | Supertest + test DB |
| E2E | Login con email, login con Google, gestión de usuarios | Playwright/Cypress |

## Migration / Rollout

1. **Phase 1**: Ejecutar migraciones de DB
2. **Phase 2**: Implementar backend auth modules
3. **Phase 3**: Implementar frontend auth pages
4. **Phase 4**: Testing integral
5. **Phase 5**: Feature flag para rollout gradual
6. **Phase 6**: Remover feature flag post-validación

**No migration required para datos existentes** - es un sistema nuevo.

## Open Questions

- [ ] ¿Usar TypeORM o Prisma para ORM?
- [ ] ¿Cuál es la estrategia de manejo de errores en frontend?
- [ ] ¿Necesitamos rate limiting para login attempts?

observations.title: sdd/smart-contract-v2/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Smart Contract v2 - Trust Work Escrow

## Intent

Crear un nuevo smart contract (v2) en Anchor/Rust que soporte multi-wallet por usuario, roles no encasillados, y pool de árbitros. El actual (v1) no tiene cuentas de usuario, solo jobs - esto limita la UX para el hackathon y un producto real.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Cuenta `User` (PDA) con múltiples wallets asociadas
- Cuenta `UserProfile` con username, bio
- Pool de árbitros registrado on-chain
- Instrucciones para gestión de wallets (add, set_active, remove)
- Instrucciones para registro de árbitros
- Migración de jobs desde v1 (mantener compatibilidad)
- Tests de integración

### Out of Scope
- Sistema de reputación/ratings (Fase 2)
- Soporte Token-2022/USDC (Fase 2)
- Gasless transactions (Fase 3)
- Frontend web/CLI (proyectos separados)

## Approach

Basado en el diseño existente en `docs/contracts/DESIGN.md`:
- User PDA: seeds = [b"user", wallet_principal]
- UserProfile PDA: seeds = [b"profile", wallet_principal]
- ArbiterPool PDA: seeds = [b"arbiter_pool"]
- Nuevo Programa ID (no es upgrade de v1, es nuevo)

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `programs/trust-escrow-v2/` | New | Nuevo programa Anchor |
| `escrow-core-v2/` | New | SDK para interacción |
| `docs/contracts/` | Updated | Specs v2 |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Complejidad alta en 4 días | Medium | Priorizar features mínimos |
| Datos de v1 no compatibles | Low | Nueva estructura, no migrate |
| Tests fallando en deadline | Medium | TDD, tests primero |

## Rollback Plan

Si el smart contract no está listo para el hackathon:
- Usar v1 desplegada actualmente (funciona, pero sin usuarios)
- Documentar como "v2 planned" para después del hackathon

## Dependencies

- Anchor CLI 0.32+
- Solana test-validator
- IDL generado para frontend

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Programa compilable con `anchor build`

observations.title: sdd/smart-contract-v2/spec
observations.content:
# Specs: Smart Contract v2 - Trust Work Escrow

## ADDED Requirements

### Domain: User Management

#### Requirement: User Account Creation

The system MUST allow any wallet to create a User account as a PDA.

- GIVEN a wallet that does not have a User account
- WHEN create_user instruction is called with username
- THEN a new User PDA is created with wallet_principal = caller, wallets_asociadas = [caller], active_wallet = caller
- AND username is stored in the account

#### Scenario: Duplicate User Creation

- GIVEN a wallet that already has a User account
- WHEN create_user is called again
- THEN the instruction MUST fail with error "User already exists"

#### Requirement: Add Secondary Wallet

The system MUST allow a User to associate additional wallets to their account.

- GIVEN a User account exists with wallet_principal = A
- WHEN add_wallet is called with new_wallet = B signed by A
- THEN wallets_asociadas MUST include B
- AND B can be set as active_wallet

#### Scenario: Add Duplicate Wallet

- GIVEN a User has wallet B already in wallets_asociadas
- WHEN add_wallet is called with wallet = B
- THEN the instruction MUST fail with error "Wallet already associated"

#### Requirement: Set Active Wallet

The system MUST allow a User to change which wallet is active for the session.

- GIVEN a User has wallets_asociadas = [A, B] and active_wallet = A
- WHEN set_active_wallet is called with wallet = B signed by A
- THEN active_wallet MUST be updated to B

#### Scenario: Set Inactive Wallet as Active

- GIVEN a User has wallets_asociadas = [A]
- WHEN set_active_wallet is called with wallet = C (not in list)
- THEN the instruction MUST fail with error "Wallet not associated"

---

### Domain: Job Management

#### Requirement: Create Job

The system MUST allow any User to create a job (only User, not arbitrary wallet).

- GIVEN a User account exists with active_wallet = A
- WHEN create_job is called with title, description, amount, deadline, arbiter
- THEN a new Job PDA is created with client = A
- AND status = Created

#### Requirement: Accept Job

The system MUST allow any User to accept a job as freelancer.

- GIVEN a Job exists with status = Funded and freelancer = None
- WHEN accept_job is called signed by User with active_wallet = F
- THEN job.freelancer MUST be set to F
- AND status MUST change to InProgress

#### Scenario: Self-Accept

- GIVEN a Job exists with client = A
- WHEN accept_job is called by User with active_wallet = A
- THEN the instruction MUST fail with error "Cannot accept own job"

#### Requirement: Submit Work

The system MUST allow the freelancer to submit completed work.

- GIVEN a Job exists with status = InProgress and freelancer = F
- WHEN submit_work is called signed by F
- THEN status MUST change to Submitted

#### Requirement: Approve Work

The system MUST allow the client to approve and release funds.

- GIVEN a Job exists with status = Submitted and client = C
- WHEN approve_work is called signed by C
- THEN freelancer receives (amount - fee)
- AND treasury receives fee * 2
- AND Job is closed

#### Requirement: Reject Work

The system MUST allow the client to reject and open dispute.

- GIVEN a Job exists with status = Submitted and client = C
- WHEN reject_work is called with reason signed by C
- THEN status MUST change to Disputed
- AND dispute_reason is stored

#### Requirement: Raise Dispute

The system MUST allow freelancer to raise dispute after submit.

- GIVEN a Job exists with status = Submitted and freelancer = F
- WHEN raise_dispute is called with reason signed by F
- THEN status MUST change to Disputed
- AND dispute_reason is stored

#### Requirement: Cancel Job

The system MUST allow client to cancel before acceptance.

- GIVEN a Job exists with status = Created or Funded and client = C
- WHEN cancel_job is called signed by C
- THEN if Funded, funds are refunded to C
- AND Job is closed with status = Cancelled

---

### Domain: Arbiter Management

#### Requirement: Register Arbiter Pool

The system MUST allow Admin to register a pool of árbitros.

- GIVEN caller is Admin (from Config)
- WHEN register_arbiters is called with list of arbiter pubkeys
- THEN ArbiterPool.arbiters MUST include all provided pubkeys

#### Requirement: Resolve Dispute

The system MUST allow a registered arbiter to resolve disputes.

- GIVEN a Job exists with status = Disputed and arbiter = A
- WHEN resolve_dispute is called with freelancer_percent signed by A
- THEN funds are distributed: freelancer gets (net_amount * percent / 100)
- AND client gets remainder
- AND treasury gets fee * 2
- AND Job is closed with status = Resolved

#### Scenario: Invalid Arbiter

- GIVEN a Job exists with arbiter = A
- WHEN resolve_dispute is called by wallet = B (not A)
- THEN the instruction MUST fail with error "Not the assigned arbiter"

---

### Domain: Governance

#### Requirement: Initialize Config

The system MUST allow initialization with admin and treasury multisig.

- GIVEN no Config account exists
- WHEN initialize_config is called with admin = [A, B, C], treasury = T, fee_percent = 5
- THEN Config is created with authority = A, treasury = T, fee_percent = 5
- AND multisig owners = [A, B, C], required = 2

#### Requirement: Pause Program

The system MUST allow Admin to pause all operations.

- GIVEN Config exists with paused = false
- WHEN pause is called signed by admin
- THEN Config.paused MUST be true

#### Requirement: Withdraw Treasury

The system MUST allow Treasury (multisig) to withdraw accumulated fees.

- GIVEN Config.treasury = T, treasury has lamports
- WHEN withdraw_treasury is called with amount signed by 2-of-3 owners
- THEN amount is transferred to recipient

---

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Job Status Flow (From v1)

The system maintains the same status flow as v1 but with User references:

| From State | Action | To State |
|------------|--------|-----------|
| Created | deposit_funds | Funded |
| Funded | accept_job | InProgress |
| InProgress | submit_work | Submitted |
| Submitted | approve_work | Released |
| Submitted | reject_work | Disputed |
| Submitted | raise_dispute | Disputed |
| Disputed | resolve_dispute | Resolved |
| Created/Funded | cancel_job | Cancelled |

---

## Out of Scope (for this spec)

- Token-2022 support (USDC)
- Reputation/ratings system
- Milestones
- Gasless transactions
- Off-chain metadata

---

## Success Criteria Verification

Each requirement MUST have at least one automated test in the test suite.

observations.title: sdd/smart-contract-v2/design
observations.content:
# Design: Smart Contract v2 - Trust Work Escrow

## Technical Approach

Nuevo programa Anchor (Rust) que extiende la funcionalidad de v1 con cuentas de usuario, multi-wallet, y pool de árbitros. No es upgrade de v1 - es un programa nuevo con su propio Program ID.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: PDA Structure

**Choice**: User PDA deriva de wallet_principal
```
seeds = [b"user", wallet_principal.as_ref()]
```
**Alternatives**: Derivar de username o sequential ID
**Rationale**: username puede tener colisiones, sequential ID requiere counter global. wallet_principal es único y seguro.

### Decision: Multi-Wallet Implementation

**Choice**: Vec<Pubkey> para wallets_asociadas + active_wallet
**Alternatives**: Separate PDA por cada wallet
**Rationale**: Simplicidad - una sola cuenta por usuario. Límite: 10 wallets max.

### Decision: Multisig Implementation

**Choice**: Threshold-based multisig (2-of-3) para admin y treasury
**Alternatives**: Programa multisig separado, or program-based multisig
**Rationale**: Anchor tiene built-in support para multisig via multiple signers en Context. Program separado agrega complejidad innecesaria.

### Decision: Arbiter Assignment

**Choice**: Arbiter seleccionado al crear job (del pool), puede cambiar a None si no hay
**Alternatives**: Auto-asignación cuando hay dispute
**Rationale**: Client conoce su proyecto y puede preferir un árbitro específico. None permite disputes sin asignar.

## Data Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        USER WORKFLOW                            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                  │
│  Wallet A                                                        │
│     │                                                            │
│     ├── create_user(username) ──► User PDA (seeds: user/A)     │
│     │                              │                             │
│     │                              ▼                             │
│     ├── add_wallet(B) ──────────► User updated                  │
│     │                              │                             │
│     ├── set_active_wallet(B) ────► active_wallet = B            │
│     │                              │                             │
│     │                              ▼                             │
│     └── create_job(...) ────────► Job PDA (seeds: job, B, id)   │
│                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `programs/trust-escrow-v2/Cargo.toml` | Create | Dependencies: anchor-lang, anchor-spl |
| `programs/trust-escrow-v2/src/lib.rs` | Create | Main program entry, declare_id! |
| `programs/trust-escrow-v2/src/error.rs` | Create | Custom error codes |
| `programs/trust-escrow-v2/src/state/` | Create | Account structs (User, Job, Config, ArbiterPool) |
| `programs/trust-escrow-v2/src/instructions/` | Create | All instruction handlers |
| `programs/trust-escrow-v2/tests/smart_contract_v2.ts` | Create | Integration tests |

## Interfaces / Contracts

### Account: User

```rust
#[account]
#[derive(InitSpace)]
pub struct User {
    pub wallet_principal: Pubkey,           // Primary wallet
    pub wallets_asociadas: Vec<Pubkey>,    // Max 10 secondary
    pub active_wallet: Pubkey,            // Current active
    pub username: String,                  // Max 32 chars
    pub bio: Option<String>,               // Max 500 chars
    pub created_at: i64,
    pub bump: u8,
}
```

### Account: Job (similar to v1 + user ref)

```rust
#[account]
#[derive(InitSpace)]
pub struct Job {
    pub client: Pubkey,                    // From User.active_wallet
    pub freelancer: Option<Pubkey>,
    pub arbiter: Option<Pubkey>,
    pub amount: u64,
    pub fee_percent: u8,
    pub fee_amount: u64,
    pub status: JobStatus,
    pub title: String,                      // Max 100
    pub description: String,                // Max 500
    pub deadline: i64,
    pub created_at: i64,
    pub updated_at: i64,
    pub dispute_reason: String,             // Max 200
    pub bump: u8,
}
```

### Account: Config

```rust
#[account]
#[derive(InitSpace)]
pub struct Config {
    pub admin: Pubkey,                      // Multisig (2-of-3)
    pub treasury: Pubkey,                  // Multisig (2-of-3)
    pub multisig_owners: Vec<Pubkey>,       // Max 5
    pub multisig_threshold: u8,             // 2 default
    pub fee_percent: u8,
    pub paused: bool,
    pub bump: u8,
}
```

### Account: ArbiterPool

```rust
#[account]
#[derive(InitSpace)]
pub struct ArbiterPool {
    pub authority: Pubkey,                  // Admin
    pub arbiters: Vec<Pubkey>,              // Max 50
    pub bump: u8,
}
```

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Unit | PDA derivation, account sizes | Rust unit tests in module |
| Integration | Instructions end-to-end | TypeScript anchor test |
| Edge Cases | Error conditions, boundary values | IT tests |

Tests prioritarios:
1. create_user + add_wallet + set_active_wallet
2. create_job + accept_job + submit_work + approve_work
3. reject_work + resolve_dispute
4. cancel_job (Funded state)
5. Multisig (2-of-3 threshold)

## Migration / Rollback

**No migration required** - Este es un programa nuevo (v2), no un upgrade de v1. Los datos de v1 viven en el programa anterior.

**Rollback**: Si el programa falla durante el hackathon, usar el programa v1 existente (ya desplegado en devnet).

## Open Questions

- [ ] ¿Cuántos bytes allocate para wallets_asociadas? (10 * 32 = 320 min)
- [ ] ¿Confirmar límite de arbiters = 50?
- [ ] ¿Necesitamos update_user instruction?
- [ ] ¿Fees en SOL o permitir futuro USDC?

## Dependencies (Rust Crates)

```toml
[dependencies]
anchor-lang = "0.32"
anchor-spl = "0.32"
solana-program = "1.18"
borsh = "0.10"
thiserror = "1.0"
```

observations.title: Session summary: Trust-Work-Escrow
observations.content:
## Goal
Build and deploy Trust Work Escrow v2 smart contract to devnet for Solana WayLearn Hackathon 2026.

## Instructions
- User works in a Docker dev container with anchor CLI installed
- Two separate filesystems: local (`/home/dcdebian/Proyects/Trust-Work-Escrow/`) and container (`/workspaces/Trust-Work-Escrow/`)
- User syncs files by copying from local to container, then restarting container
- After each fix, user runs `anchor build` in container and reports results
- Container resets frequently, so files must be kept in local

## Discoveries

### Project Structure Issues - FIXED
**Problem**: V2 had files in wrong locations, causing build issues.
- `target/` folder was inside `programs/trust-escrow-v2/` instead of project root
- `Cargo.lock` was inside `programs/trust-escrow-v2/` instead of project root
- Missing `Cargo.toml` in project root (workspace file)
- Extra `src/instructions/` and `src/state/` folders that weren't needed

**Solution**: Aligned V2 structure to match V1 (reference):
```
trust-escrow-v2/
├── Anchor.toml
├── Cargo.toml              ← Workspace file (NEW)
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── rust-toolchain.toml
├── migrations/
├── programs/
│   └── trust-escrow-v2/
│       ├── Cargo.toml
│       └── src/
│           └── lib.rs
└── tests/
```

### Missing Cargo.toml [lib] Section - FIXED
**Problem**: `cargo build` compiled but didn't generate `.so` file.
**Solution**: Added `[lib]` section to `programs/trust-escrow-v2/Cargo.toml`:
```toml
[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib", "lib"]
name = "trust_escrow_v2"
```

### Solana Test Validator - NOT WORKING
**Problem**: Test validator crashes due to `io_uring` not supported in container kernel.
Error: `assertion failed: io_uring_supported()`
**Workaround**: Using devnet for testing instead of local validator.

### Files Added to V2
- `migrations/deploy.ts`
- `rust-toolchain.toml`
- `.gitignore`
- `.prettierignore`
- `Cargo.toml` (workspace root file)
- `.mocharc.json`
- `tsconfig.json`
- Updated `package.json` and `tests/trust-escrow-v2.ts`

## Accomplished
- ✅ Fixed project structure (matched V1)
- ✅ Fixed Cargo.toml with `[lib]` section
- ✅ Added all missing configuration files
- ✅ Rewrote tests to match smart contract API
- ✅ Configured devnet in Anchor.toml

## Next Steps
1. User needs to COPY files from local to container:
   ```bash
   cp -r /home/dcdebian/Proyects/Trust-Work-Escrow/trust-escrow-v2/* /workspaces/Trust-Work-Escrow/trust-escrow-v2/
   ```
2. Clean and build:
   ```bash
   cd /workspaces/Trust-Work-Escrow/trust-escrow-v2
   rm -rf target
   anchor build
   ```
3. Deploy to devnet:
   ```bash
   anchor deploy
   ```
4. Run tests:
   ```bash
   anchor test
   ```

## Relevant Files

### Local filesystem:
```
/home/dcdebian/Proyects/Trust-Work-Escrow/trust-escrow-v2/
├── Anchor.toml (devnet configured)
├── Cargo.toml (workspace file)
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── rust-toolchain.toml
├── migrations/deploy.ts
├── programs/trust-escrow-v2/
│   ├── Cargo.toml (with [lib] section)
│   └── src/
│       ├── lib.rs (535 lines - complete smart contract)
│       └── error.rs
└── tests/
    └── trust-escrow-v2.ts (rewritten tests)
```

### Program ID
`38ateWCzE9dDmE1CxqPJ22T4pr3WRQbgjc9Z4uv69TkP`

## Key Code Patterns

### Seeds used in accounts:
- Config: `seeds = [b"config"]`
- User: `seeds = [b"user", authority.key().as_ref()]`
- Job: `seeds = [b"job", client.key().as_ref()]`
- ArbiterPool: `seeds = [b"arbiter_pool"]`

### Status values (u8 constants):
- STATUS_CREATED = 0
- STATUS_FUNDED = 1
- STATUS_IN_PROGRESS = 2
- STATUS_SUBMITTED = 3
- STATUS_COMPLETED = 4
- STATUS_CANCELLED = 5
- STATUS_DISPUTED = 6

observations.title: sdd/core-library/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: Core Library Epic for Trust Work Escrow v2

### Current State

**v1 Implementation Analysis (trust-escrow/escrow-core/)**:
- Single Rust crate with 1,318 lines implementing complete Solana operations
- 29 public functions covering full job lifecycle
- Manual borsh deserialization and instruction building
- Raw RPC client operations without type safety
- Limited to v1 smart contract functionality (basic jobs without teams, milestones, disputes)

**v2 Smart Contract Status**:
- Complete Anchor 0.32 program with 31 instructions implemented
- Modern architecture with Users, Teams, Jobs, Disputes, Milestones, Treasury
- Generated IDL with 2,778 lines providing full type definitions
- All 4 phases complete (Setup, Jobs/Teams, Disputes/Milestones/Treasury, Tests)
- Monolithic lib.rs structure due to Anchor 0.32 module bug

### Affected Areas

- `trust-escrow-v2/target/idl/trust_escrow_v2.json` — Generated IDL with complete type definitions
- `trust-escrow-v2/tests/trust-escrow-v2.ts` — Reference TypeScript client patterns
- `trust-escrow/escrow-core/src/lib.rs` — v1 implementation for architectural reference
- `trust-escrow-v2/programs/trust-escrow-v2/src/lib.rs` — Smart contract with 31 instructions
- New core library location (to be determined)

### Approaches

1. **Pure Rust Library (v1 Evolution)**
   - Pros: Maximum performance, native Solana integration, familiar to v1 users
   - Cons: TypeScript ecosystem can't use directly, limited web integration
   - Effort: Medium (adapt v1 patterns to v2 smart contract)

2. **TypeScript-First Library**
   - Pros: Generated from IDL, web-native, better DX for frontend/backend, npm ecosystem
   - Cons: Node.js only, no native Rust performance benefits
   - Effort: Low (leverage Anchor's generated TypeScript client)

3. **Dual Language Support (Rust + TypeScript)**
   - Pros: Best of both worlds, maximum ecosystem coverage
   - Cons: Maintenance overhead, API synchronization challenges
   - Effort: High (two separate implementations)

4. **WebAssembly Bridge (Rust → WASM → JS)**
   - Pros: Single Rust implementation, web compatibility, near-native performance
   - Cons: WASM complexity, bundle size, async/Promise wrapping overhead
   - Effort: High (WASM bindings and packaging)

5. **Anchor Client + Rust Wrapper Hybrid**
   - Pros: Leverages Anchor's type generation, adds Rust convenience layer
   - Cons: Complex API surface, potential version drift
   - Effort: Medium-High

### Recommendation

**TypeScript-First Library** (Approach #2) with future Rust compatibility layer.

**Rationale**:
1. **Leverage Anchor Ecosystem**: The generated IDL and TypeScript client provide immediate type safety and SDK
2. **Web-First Strategy**: All planned consumers (Backend API, CLI/TUI, Frontend) can use TypeScript/Node.js
3. **Rapid Development**: Anchor 0.32 generates mature client code automatically
4. **Future-Proof**: Rust wrapper can be added later if performance becomes critical

**Core Library Architecture**:
```typescript
escrow-core-v2/
├── src/
│   ├── client.ts           // High-level escrow operations
│   ├── accounts.ts         // PDA derivation helpers
│   ├── instructions.ts     // Instruction builders
│   ├── types.ts            // Generated + custom types
│   └── utils.ts            // Common utilities
├── generated/              // Anchor-generated client
└── tests/                  // Unit tests
```

### Risks

- **Type Safety Dependencies**: Relying on Anchor IDL generation quality
- **Performance Concerns**: TypeScript may be slower than Rust for high-frequency operations
- **Breaking Changes**: Anchor version upgrades could affect generated client
- **Bundle Size**: Full Anchor client might be heavy for frontend use

### Integration Points with v2 Smart Contract

**Required Adaptations from v1**:
1. **User Management**: Add user profile creation and wallet management
2. **Team Operations**: Support team creation and member management  
3. **Enhanced Job Lifecycle**: Include application/acceptance flow
4. **Milestone Support**: Add milestone creation and approval operations
5. **Dispute System**: Implement dispute raising and resolution
6. **Multi-signature**: Support multisig operations for enterprise accounts

**New Capabilities Not in v1**:
- User profiles with multi-wallet support (up to 5 wallets)
- Team-based freelancer collaboration
- Milestone-based payment releases
- Structured dispute resolution with arbiter pools
- Treasury management and fee collection

### Ready for Proposal

**Yes** - Clear architecture decision made with sufficient analysis.

The orchestrator should tell the user: "Core Library exploration complete. Recommendation: TypeScript-first library leveraging Anchor's generated client for rapid development and web ecosystem compatibility. Ready to proceed with detailed proposal and implementation planning."

observations.content:
# Proposal: Core Library v2 Integration

## Intent

Replace legacy escrow-core library with modern Rust SDK crate leveraging the completed v2 smart contract. Current v1 library (1,318 lines) uses outdated patterns and incompatible PDAs. New Rust SDK must support all 31 v2 contract instructions while providing type-safe, high-level operations for CLI, TUI, and backend consumption as a publishable crates.io package.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Rust SDK crate using Anchor-generated client types
- High-level escrow operations (users, teams, jobs, disputes, milestones)
- PDA derivation helpers matching v2 contract patterns
- Instruction builders with proper validation
- Multi-wallet architecture support (CLI/TUI/Backend integration)
- Publishable on crates.io with comprehensive documentation
- Integration patterns for Anchor Rust client

### Out of Scope
- Smart contract modifications (already completed)
- CLI/TUI implementation (Epic #4)
- Backend API layer (Epic #3)
- Frontend implementation (Epic #5)

## Approach

**Rust-First Architecture**: Build around Anchor-generated Rust client types rather than manual definitions. Leverage generated code for instruction schemas and account structures.

**Layered Design**:
- `client.rs` - CofreClient for high-level operations wrapping instruction sequences
- `instructions.rs` - Instruction builders with validation
- `pda.rs` - PDA derivation utilities matching v2 patterns
- `types.rs` - Account types and enums extending generated ones
- `error.rs` - Error handling and result types
- `lib.rs` - Public API exports and crate organization

**Integration Strategy**: Consume Anchor-generated Rust client without modifications. Use established PDA seeds and account relationships from v2 smart contract.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `sdk/` | New | Complete Rust SDK crate package |
| `programs/trust-escrow-v2/` | Read | Anchor client generation source |
| `Cargo.toml` | Modified | Add workspace member and dependencies |
| Legacy `escrow-core/` | Deprecated | Mark for removal post-migration |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Anchor client generation issues | Low | Pin to specific Anchor version, test generation |
| PDA derivation mismatches with v2 | Medium | Comprehensive integration tests against deployed contract |
| Cargo dependency conflicts | Low | Careful version management, lockfile tracking |
| Breaking changes to consuming Rust services | High | Semantic versioning, migration guide, compatibility layer |

## Rollback Plan

1. Revert `Cargo.toml` workspace changes
2. Remove `sdk/` directory
3. Restore legacy `escrow-core` as primary library
4. Update any modified import statements in consuming Rust services
5. Smart contract remains unchanged

## Dependencies

- Completed v2 smart contract with stable Anchor client generation
- Anchor framework 0.32+ Rust client features
- Rust 1.75+ for modern language features
- Solana SDK compatibility for transaction building

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 31 v2 contract instructions accessible via CofreClient
- [ ] PDA derivation matches contract implementation 100%
- [ ] Unit test coverage >90% with integration test suite
- [ ] Crate builds successfully and passes clippy/fmt checks
- [ ] Documentation covers all public APIs with usage examples
- [ ] Published to crates.io with proper versioning
- [ ] CLI, TUI, and Backend can consume SDK without breaking changes
- [ ] Migration guide from v1 escrow-core available

observations.title: sdd/core-library/design
observations.content:
# Design: Core Library v2 Integration

## Technical Approach

Build a modern Rust SDK crate that wraps the completed v2 smart contract, providing type-safe, high-level operations through auto-generated Anchor client types. Replace legacy escrow-core (1,318 lines) with structured SDK that supports all 31 v2 instructions while serving CLI, TUI, and backend integrations as a publishable crates.io package.

The approach leverages Anchor's client generation to avoid manual type definitions, uses established PDA patterns from v2 contract, and implements builder patterns for complex multi-instruction operations.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: Anchor Client Integration Strategy

**Choice**: Consume Anchor-generated types via build.rs + IDL without modifications
**Alternatives considered**: Manual type definitions, fork Anchor client, copy-paste generated code
**Rationale**: Generated types ensure 100% compatibility with contract changes, reduce maintenance overhead, and provide compile-time safety. build.rs approach keeps codebase clean while ensuring types stay current.

### Decision: Crate Structure - Layered API Design

**Choice**: Layered architecture: low-level instructions → high-level client → domain operations
**Alternatives considered**: Single flat module, feature-based modules, procedural API
**Rationale**: Matches existing patterns in Solana ecosystem, allows progressive disclosure of complexity, enables power users to use instruction builders while providing convenient high-level operations.

### Decision: PDA Management Strategy

**Choice**: Centralized PDA derivation with caching via lazy_static HashMap
**Alternatives considered**: On-demand derivation, client instance caching, no caching
**Rationale**: PDA derivation is CPU-intensive, frequently repeated, and deterministic. Central cache reduces redundant computation while maintaining thread safety.

### Decision: Error Handling Pattern

**Choice**: Custom Error enum wrapping Anchor/Solana errors with context
**Alternatives considered**: Re-export upstream errors, anyhow::Error throughout, Result aliases
**Rationale**: Provides semantic error types for consuming applications while preserving underlying error details. Enables better error handling in CLI/TUI layers.

### Decision: Async Runtime Integration

**Choice**: Runtime-agnostic with tokio feature flag (default enabled)
**Alternatives considered**: Hard tokio dependency, runtime abstraction layer, sync-only API
**Rationale**: CLI and TUI both use tokio, but library should be flexible. Feature flag allows opt-out while default behavior supports primary use cases.

## Data Flow

```
CLI/TUI/Backend
      │
      ▼
CofreClient (high-level operations)
      │
      ▼
InstructionBuilder (validation + construction)
      │
      ▼  
Generated Anchor Client (type-safe instructions)
      │
      ▼
Solana RPC Client → v2 Smart Contract
```

**PDA Flow**:
```
Operation Request → PDA Cache Check → Derive if Missing → Cache Result → Use in Transaction
```

**Error Flow**:
```
Solana/Anchor Error → Custom Error Context → Result<T, EscrowError> → Application Layer
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `sdk/Cargo.toml` | Create | SDK crate manifest with Anchor client deps |
| `sdk/build.rs` | Create | Anchor IDL client generation at build time |
| `sdk/src/lib.rs` | Create | Public API exports and crate organization |
| `sdk/src/client.rs` | Create | CofreClient high-level operations wrapper |
| `sdk/src/instructions.rs` | Create | All 31 instruction builders with validation |
| `sdk/src/pda.rs` | Create | PDA derivation utilities with caching |
| `sdk/src/types.rs` | Create | Account structs and enums extending generated |
| `sdk/src/error.rs` | Create | Custom error types and conversions |
| `sdk/src/utils.rs` | Create | Helper functions and utilities |
| `sdk/examples/` | Create | Usage examples and integration patterns |
| `sdk/tests/` | Create | Integration test suite |
| `Cargo.toml` (root) | Create | Workspace configuration adding SDK member |

## Interfaces / Contracts

### CofreClient Interface
```rust
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct CofreClient {
    rpc: Arc<RpcClient>,
    payer: Arc<dyn Signer>,
    commitment: CommitmentConfig,
}

impl CofreClient {
    // High-level operations
    pub async fn create_user(&self, username: &str, bio: Option<&str>) -> Result<Signature>;
    pub async fn create_job(&self, job_params: CreateJobParams) -> Result<(Pubkey, Signature)>;
    pub async fn apply_to_job(&self, job: Pubkey, proposal: &str) -> Result<Signature>;
    
    // Multi-instruction operations  
    pub async fn complete_job_workflow(&self, job: Pubkey) -> Result<Vec<Signature>>;
    pub async fn resolve_dispute(&self, dispute: Pubkey, resolution: DisputeResolution) -> Result<Signature>;
}
```

### PDA Derivation Interface
```rust
pub struct PdaCache {
    config: LazyLock<Pubkey>,
    users: LazyLock<DashMap<Pubkey, Pubkey>>,
    jobs: LazyLock<DashMap<(Pubkey, u64), Pubkey>>,
}

pub fn derive_user_pda(authority: &Pubkey) -> (Pubkey, u8);
pub fn derive_job_pda(client: &Pubkey, job_id: u64) -> (Pubkey, u8);
pub fn derive_dispute_pda(job: &Pubkey) -> (Pubkey, u8);
```

### Error Type Interface
```rust
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum EscrowError {
    #[error("Anchor error: {0}")]
    Anchor(#[from] anchor_client::ClientError),
    #[error("Solana error: {0}")]
    Solana(#[from] solana_client::client_error::ClientError),
    #[error("Invalid parameter: {msg}")]
    InvalidParameter { msg: String },
    #[error("Contract error: {code} - {msg}")]
    Contract { code: u32, msg: String },
}
```

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Unit | PDA derivation correctness | Property tests against known seeds |
| Unit | Instruction validation logic | Invalid input rejection tests |
| Unit | Error handling and conversion | Mock error propagation tests |
| Integration | End-to-end instruction execution | Local validator with deployed contract |
| Integration | Multi-instruction workflows | Complex scenario testing |
| Integration | RPC client configuration | Network timeout and retry behavior |

## Migration / Rollout

**Phase 1**: SDK development and testing against v2 contract
- Build SDK crate with comprehensive test coverage
- Validate against deployed v2 contract on local validator
- Performance benchmark against legacy escrow-core

**Phase 2**: Gradual integration
- CLI migration: Replace escrow-core imports with SDK
- TUI migration: Update state management to use SDK types  
- Backend integration: Add SDK as dependency

**Phase 3**: Legacy deprecation
- Mark escrow-core as deprecated
- Remove from workspace members
- Update documentation and examples

No data migration required - SDK consumes same on-chain state.

## Open Questions

- [ ] Should SDK include transaction retry logic or leave to consuming applications?
- [ ] PDA cache invalidation strategy for long-running applications?
- [ ] Anchor IDL version compatibility guarantees across SDK versions?
- [ ] SDK versioning strategy relative to smart contract versions?

observations.content:
# Core Library v2 Specification

## Purpose
Specifications for TypeScript-first Rust SDK Core Library that replaces legacy escrow-core with v2 smart contract integration.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: CofreClient High-Level Interface

The CofreClient MUST provide a high-level TypeScript interface wrapping all v2 contract operations with type-safe, async methods for job lifecycle management.

#### Scenario: Client Initialization
- GIVEN a Solana RPC endpoint and wallet adapter
- WHEN CofreClient is instantiated
- THEN it MUST connect to v2 contract and expose typed methods
- AND it MUST validate program ID matches deployed v2 contract

#### Scenario: Job Lifecycle Operations
- GIVEN an authenticated client instance
- WHEN job lifecycle operations are executed (create → fund → apply → accept → submit → approve)
- THEN each step MUST enforce proper state transitions per JobStatus enum
- AND all operations MUST return typed responses with transaction signatures

### Requirement: PDA Derivation Utilities

The SDK MUST provide PDA derivation helpers matching v2 contract seed patterns for all account types.

#### Scenario: Account PDA Generation
- GIVEN account type (Config, User, Job, Team, ArbiterPool, Dispute, Milestone) and required seeds
- WHEN deriving PDA addresses
- THEN addresses MUST match contract implementation exactly
- AND seed patterns MUST be: Config("config"), User("user", authority), Job("job", client, job_id), Team("team", owner), ArbiterPool("arbiter_pool"), Dispute("dispute", job), Milestone("milestone", job, index)

### Requirement: Type System Integration

The SDK MUST provide comprehensive TypeScript types extending Anchor-generated IDL types with additional business logic validation.

#### Scenario: Account Type Definitions
- GIVEN v2 contract account structures (Config, User, Job, Team, ArbiterPool, Dispute, Milestone)
- WHEN consuming account data
- THEN types MUST include all fields with proper TypeScript mapping
- AND enums MUST match contract definitions (JobStatus, ApplicationStatus, MemberRole, DisputeStatus, MilestoneStatus)

#### Scenario: Instruction Builder Validation
- GIVEN instruction parameters for any of the 31 v2 contract instructions
- WHEN building instructions
- THEN validation MUST occur before transaction creation
- AND errors MUST use custom error types matching contract ErrorCode enum

### Requirement: Multi-Wallet Architecture Support

The SDK MUST support multi-wallet scenarios with up to 5 wallets per user account and proper wallet management operations.

#### Scenario: Wallet Association Management
- GIVEN a User account with existing wallets
- WHEN adding new wallet via add_wallet instruction
- THEN validation MUST enforce MAX_WALLETS (5) limit
- AND wallet uniqueness MUST be validated before association

#### Scenario: Active Wallet Switching
- GIVEN a User account with multiple associated wallets
- WHEN switching active wallet via set_active_wallet
- THEN new wallet MUST be in user's wallet list
- AND subsequent operations MUST use new active wallet for authorization

### Requirement: Complete Instruction Coverage

The SDK MUST provide instruction builders for all 31 v2 contract instructions with proper account resolution and parameter validation.

#### Scenario: Config Instructions (5)
- GIVEN admin authority
- WHEN calling initialize_config, pause, unpause, withdraw_treasury, update_treasury
- THEN instructions MUST include proper multisig validation
- AND treasury operations MUST enforce admin authorization

#### Scenario: User Management Instructions (4)
- GIVEN user authority
- WHEN calling create_user, add_wallet, set_active_wallet, update_user
- THEN validation MUST enforce username length (32), bio length (500), max wallets (5)
- AND wallet operations MUST validate wallet ownership

#### Scenario: Team Instructions (2)
- GIVEN team owner authority
- WHEN calling create_team, add_team_member
- THEN team name/description MUST enforce length limits
- AND member roles MUST validate against MemberRole enum

#### Scenario: Job Lifecycle Instructions (8)
- GIVEN client/freelancer authority as appropriate
- WHEN calling create_job, deposit_funds, apply_to_job, accept_application, submit_work, approve_work, reject_work, cancel_job
- THEN job state transitions MUST follow JobStatus workflow
- AND amount validations MUST enforce MIN_JOB_AMOUNT (100,000 lamports)

#### Scenario: Arbiter Pool Instructions (3)
- GIVEN admin authority
- WHEN calling create_arbiter_pool, add_arbiter, remove_arbiter
- THEN arbiter count MUST enforce MAX_ARBITERS (50) limit
- AND arbiter validation MUST check authority permissions

#### Scenario: Dispute Instructions (5)
- GIVEN authorized dispute participants
- WHEN calling raise_dispute, submit_evidence, assign_arbiter, resolve_dispute, finalize_dispute_payouts
- THEN evidence MUST enforce MAX_DISPUTE_EVIDENCE (2048 chars)
- AND payout percentages MUST sum to 100%

#### Scenario: Milestone Instructions (4)
- GIVEN job client/freelancer
- WHEN calling create_milestone, submit_milestone, approve_milestone, reject_milestone
- THEN milestone count MUST enforce MAX_MILESTONES (20) per job
- AND milestone amounts MUST validate against job total

### Requirement: Integration Pattern Support

The SDK MUST provide integration patterns optimized for CLI, TUI (Ratatui), and Backend (Axum) consumers.

#### Scenario: CLI Integration Pattern
- GIVEN command-line consumer environment
- WHEN executing escrow operations
- THEN SDK MUST provide simplified CLI-friendly interfaces
- AND error messages MUST be human-readable for terminal output

#### Scenario: TUI Integration Pattern  
- GIVEN Ratatui TUI consumer
- WHEN displaying escrow state and handling user interactions
- THEN SDK MUST provide reactive state patterns compatible with Ratatui widgets
- AND async operations MUST integrate with TUI event loops

#### Scenario: Backend Integration Pattern
- GIVEN Axum web service consumer
- WHEN handling HTTP API requests
- THEN SDK MUST provide service-layer patterns with proper error handling
- AND operations MUST be compatible with async web handler patterns

### Requirement: Comprehensive Error Handling

The SDK MUST provide custom error types mapping all v2 contract errors with additional client-side validations.

#### Scenario: Contract Error Mapping
- GIVEN any v2 contract error (UserAlreadyExists, WalletAlreadyAssociated, etc.)
- WHEN error occurs during instruction execution
- THEN SDK MUST map to appropriate custom error type
- AND error messages MUST provide actionable information

#### Scenario: Client-Side Validation
- GIVEN invalid parameters before instruction execution
- WHEN validation fails
- THEN SDK MUST throw validation errors before sending transaction
- AND validation MUST cover all business logic constraints

### Requirement: Test Coverage and Documentation

The SDK MUST include comprehensive unit tests (>90% coverage) and documentation with examples for all public APIs.

#### Scenario: Unit Test Coverage
- GIVEN any public API method or utility function
- WHEN running test suite
- THEN coverage MUST exceed 90% for all modules
- AND tests MUST cover both success and error scenarios

#### Scenario: API Documentation
- GIVEN any public interface (CofreClient methods, PDA utilities, types)
- WHEN developer consumes the SDK
- THEN documentation MUST include TypeScript examples and parameter descriptions
- AND migration guide from v1 escrow-core MUST be provided

### Requirement: Package Distribution

The SDK MUST build successfully for both Node.js and browser targets with proper tree-shaking support and crates.io publication readiness.

#### Scenario: Multi-Target Builds
- GIVEN TypeScript source code
- WHEN building for distribution
- THEN packages MUST generate separate Node.js and browser bundles
- AND browser bundle MUST support tree-shaking for frontend optimization

#### Scenario: Crates.io Publication
- GIVEN completed SDK implementation
- WHEN preparing for publication
- THEN package structure MUST meet crates.io requirements
- AND all dependencies MUST be properly declared with version constraints

## Exploration: Epic #3 - CLI/TUI Applications

### Current State

The Trust Work Escrow v2 project has a solid foundation for Epic #3:

#### Available Foundation
- **Epic #2 SDK**: Complete with 51 operations covering all escrow functionality (user management, jobs, teams, disputes, milestones)
- **Legacy CLI/TUI**: Existing applications in `trust-escrow/cli` and `trust-escrow/tui` using the v1 `escrow-core` library
- **Architecture Patterns**: Established Ratatui app structure with proper terminal handling, event loops, and logging
- **Dependency Stack**: Proven combinations of `clap` + `tokio` for CLI and `ratatui` + `crossterm` for TUI
- **Documentation**: Comprehensive Epic #3 plan already written with detailed structure and success criteria

#### Technical Foundation Available
- SDK provides 51 async operations with proper error handling
- Type-safe interfaces for all account types (User, Job, Team, Dispute, Milestone)
- Performance optimized SDK with caching, retry logic, and batch operations
- Example code showing integration patterns (`simple-escrow.rs`)
- Multi-wallet support and user role management

### Affected Areas

- `trust-escrow-v2/` — New CLI/TUI applications will be created here
- `trust-escrow-v2/Cargo.toml` — Workspace will need to include CLI/TUI members  
- `trust-escrow-v2/sdk/` — Integration point for both applications
- Legacy `trust-escrow/cli/` and `trust-escrow/tui/` — Reference implementations for architecture patterns
- `docs/planning/epic-cli-tui/` — Existing epic documentation provides roadmap

### Approaches

#### 1. **Clean Rewrite Approach** — Build v2 CLI/TUI from scratch with SDK
- **Pros**: 
  - Clean integration with v2 SDK and its 51 operations
  - Modern architecture aligned with Epic #2 patterns
  - No technical debt from v1 escrow-core library
  - Opportunity to implement all documented Epic #3 features
  - Better error handling and performance optimization
- **Cons**: 
  - More development time required
  - Need to reimplement proven UI/UX patterns from legacy versions
- **Effort**: High

#### 2. **Migration Approach** — Port existing CLI/TUI to use v2 SDK
- **Pros**:
  - Faster initial implementation by reusing proven interface designs
  - Established user flows and command structures
  - Working Ratatui app architecture and terminal handling
- **Cons**:
  - Technical debt from v1 architecture patterns
  - May not fully leverage v2 SDK capabilities (like milestones, advanced dispute handling)
  - Legacy code may not align with Epic #3 comprehensive feature requirements
- **Effort**: Medium

#### 3. **Hybrid Approach** — New applications with legacy UX/architecture reference
- **Pros**:
  - Best of both: clean v2 SDK integration with proven UX patterns
  - Can cherry-pick the best architectural decisions from legacy apps
  - Allows full implementation of Epic #3 features while learning from v1
  - Meets hackathon demo requirements effectively
- **Cons**:
  - Requires analysis of both codebases
  - Potentially longer design phase
- **Effort**: Medium-High

### Recommendation

**Hybrid Approach** is optimal for Epic #3 given the hackathon constraints and demo requirements:

#### Implementation Strategy
1. **CLI Foundation**: New `trust-escrow-v2/cli/` using Clap with command structure inspired by legacy CLI but extended for v2 SDK operations

- **Time Efficiency**: Learning from legacy UX while building clean v2 integration
- **Comprehensive Coverage**: All 51 SDK operations accessible through intuitive interfaces
- **Real-time Demo**: Live Solana transactions with visual feedback for judges

- **Timeline Risk**: Hackathon deadline March 25, 2026 requires efficient execution across 32 tasks
- **Complexity Risk**: TUI applications with real-time Solana data require careful async state management
- **Integration Risk**: Need to ensure SDK integration patterns are thoroughly tested for demo reliability
- **User Experience Risk**: Terminal applications must be intuitive enough for hackathon judges to test interactively

observations.content:
# Proposal: Epic #3 - CLI/TUI Applications

## Intent

Build compelling CLI and TUI applications showcasing the complete Trust Work Escrow protocol for the March 25 hackathon demo. Enable freelancers, clients, and arbiters to interact with all 51 SDK operations through intuitive terminal interfaces, demonstrating real Solana transactions with visual feedback to impress judges and establish foundation for future backend development.

## Scope

### In Scope
- **Trust Escrow CLI**: Full-featured command-line interface for all user workflows (job management, payments, disputes, milestones)
- **Trust Escrow TUI**: Rich terminal interface with real-time Solana data visualization and interactive navigation
- **User Role Support**: Freelancer, client, and arbiter workflows with role-specific dashboards and operations
- **Live Demo Integration**: Devnet transactions with visual feedback suitable for hackathon presentation
- **SDK Integration**: All 51 operations accessible through clean, documented interfaces

### Out of Scope
- Web/mobile interfaces (Epic #4)
- Production deployment infrastructure (Epic #4)
- Advanced analytics beyond basic metrics
- Custom branding/themes (focus on functionality over aesthetics)

## Approach

**Hybrid Strategy**: New v2 applications with proven UX patterns from legacy reference implementations.

**Technical Architecture**:
- `trust-escrow-v2/cli/` - Clap-based CLI with subcommands matching SDK operations
- `trust-escrow-v2/tui/` - Ratatui application with async state management for real-time updates
- Shared core module for common SDK integration patterns
- Comprehensive error handling with user-friendly messaging
- Configuration management for multiple Solana environments (localnet/devnet)

**User Experience Strategy**:
- CLI: Intuitive command structure (`twe job create`, `twe milestone complete`)
- TUI: Dashboard approach with tabbed interfaces for different user roles
- Real-time feedback for blockchain operations with progress indicators
- Help system and command discovery features

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `trust-escrow-v2/cli/` | New | Command-line interface application |
| `trust-escrow-v2/tui/` | New | Terminal user interface application |
| `trust-escrow-v2/Cargo.toml` | Modified | Add CLI/TUI workspace members |
| `trust-escrow-v2/sdk/` | Referenced | Integration point for both applications |
| `docs/` | Extended | CLI/TUI usage documentation |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Hackathon deadline pressure | High | Use proven architecture patterns from legacy apps, focus on core demo features first |
| TUI async complexity | Medium | Leverage existing Ratatui patterns, thorough testing with mock data before live integration |
| SDK integration issues | Low | Epic #2 complete with comprehensive tests, use existing example patterns |
| Demo environment stability | Medium | Test extensively on devnet, have localnet fallback prepared |

## Rollback Plan

If complexity exceeds timeline:
1. **Minimum Viable Demo**: CLI-only version with core operations (job create, accept, complete)
2. **Simplified TUI**: Static interface without real-time updates, manual refresh
3. **Mock Data Mode**: Pre-populated demo data instead of live blockchain calls
4. **Legacy Fallback**: Use existing v1 applications with manual Epic #2 SDK demonstration

## Dependencies

- Epic #2 SDK (✅ Complete - 51 operations available)
- Solana devnet stability for live demo
- Existing legacy CLI/TUI applications as UX reference
- Ratatui/Clap ecosystem stability

## Success Criteria

- [ ] CLI application supports all user workflows with comprehensive help system
- [ ] TUI application provides real-time Solana data visualization
- [ ] Both applications successfully demonstrate live devnet transactions
- [ ] All 51 SDK operations accessible through either interface
- [ ] Demo-ready with compelling visual presentation for hackathon judges
- [ ] Clean integration patterns documented for Epic #4 backend development
- [ ] Complete user workflows: job creation → milestone tracking → payment completion
- [ ] Error handling provides clear, actionable feedback to users

observations.content:
# Specifications: Epic #3 - CLI/TUI Applications

## CLI Application Specification

### Purpose
Provide command-line interface for all Trust Work Escrow operations with comprehensive user workflow support.

### Requirements

#### Requirement: Command Structure
The CLI MUST implement hierarchical command structure matching user workflows.

**Scenario: User discovers available commands**
- GIVEN user runs `twe --help`
- WHEN command executes
- THEN system displays top-level command categories (user, job, milestone, payment, dispute)
- AND displays global options (--network, --wallet, --config)

**Scenario: User accesses subcommand help**
- GIVEN user runs `twe job --help`
- WHEN command executes  
- THEN system displays all job-related commands with usage examples
- AND displays required/optional parameters with descriptions

#### Requirement: User Management
The CLI MUST support complete user lifecycle operations.

**Scenario: Create new user profile**
- GIVEN user runs `twe user create --type freelancer --name "Alice" --skills "rust,solana"`
- WHEN command executes
- THEN system creates user profile on-chain
- AND displays confirmation with user ID
- AND stores profile locally for future operations

**Scenario: Add wallet to existing user**
- GIVEN existing user profile
- WHEN user runs `twe user add-wallet --address ABC123...`
- THEN system associates wallet with user profile
- AND validates wallet signature ownership

#### Requirement: Job Lifecycle
The CLI MUST support complete job workflow from creation to completion.

**Scenario: Client creates new job**
- GIVEN user profile exists with client role
- WHEN user runs `twe job create --title "Smart Contract Dev" --budget 1000 --duration 30`
- THEN system creates job posting on-chain
- AND generates unique job ID
- AND displays job details for confirmation

**Scenario: Freelancer applies to job**
- GIVEN active job posting exists
- WHEN freelancer runs `twe job apply --job-id J123 --proposal "I can deliver this in 25 days"`
- THEN system submits application on-chain
- AND notifies client of new application

#### Requirement: Error Handling
The CLI MUST provide clear, actionable error messages for all failure scenarios.

**Scenario: Invalid wallet configuration**
- GIVEN misconfigured or missing wallet
- WHEN user attempts any blockchain operation
- THEN system displays wallet setup instructions
- AND suggests specific configuration commands

**Scenario: Network connectivity issues**
- GIVEN Solana network unavailable
- WHEN user attempts blockchain operation
- THEN system displays network status and retry options
- AND suggests alternative network configurations

## TUI Application Specification

### Purpose
Provide rich terminal interface with real-time data visualization for complex workflow management.

### Requirements

#### Requirement: Multi-Panel Dashboard
The TUI MUST implement role-specific dashboards with organized information panels.

**Scenario: Freelancer dashboard view**
- GIVEN freelancer user launches TUI
- WHEN application starts
- THEN system displays three-panel layout: jobs browser, active projects, notifications
- AND highlights actionable items requiring freelancer attention

**Scenario: Client dashboard view**
- GIVEN client user launches TUI  
- WHEN application starts
- THEN system displays panels: posted jobs, applications received, project progress
- AND shows payment status and milestone tracking

#### Requirement: Real-Time Updates
The TUI MUST display live blockchain data with automatic refresh.

**Scenario: Transaction status monitoring**
- GIVEN user initiated blockchain transaction
- WHEN transaction is processing
- THEN system displays progress indicator with transaction hash
- AND updates status when confirmed/failed
- AND shows final transaction details

**Scenario: Job application notifications**
- GIVEN client has posted job
- WHEN freelancer submits application
- THEN client TUI automatically displays new application notification
- AND highlights application in pending review list

#### Requirement: Interactive Navigation
The TUI MUST support keyboard navigation and contextual actions.

**Scenario: Job browsing navigation**
- GIVEN jobs list displayed
- WHEN user presses up/down arrows
- THEN system highlights different jobs
- AND pressing Enter shows detailed job view
- AND 'a' key triggers application workflow

**Scenario: Milestone interaction**
- GIVEN project with milestones displayed
- WHEN user navigates to milestone and presses Enter
- THEN system shows milestone details and available actions
- AND provides context-sensitive help for current state

## Integration Specification

### Purpose
Define seamless integration patterns with Epic #2 SDK and user experience requirements.

### Requirements

#### Requirement: SDK Operation Coverage
