observations.title: OpenTUI plugin: signal-touching helpers must live inside createRoot closure
observations.content:
**What**: In tts-monitor.tsx, `fetchVoices` was defined at module scope but called `setVoices` (a Solid signal setter created inside `createRoot`). That threw a swallowed ReferenceError (caught by `catch {}`), so the OS voice list never populated and the voice selector only showed "Sistema (default)".
**Why**: Solid signals/setters are closure-scoped to the `createRoot((disposeRoot) => {...})` callback; module-scope functions cannot see them.
**Where**: src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx
**Learned**: Any helper that touches plugin signals (setVoices, setVoice, poll, etc.) MUST be defined INSIDE the createRoot closure, like speakText/bridgeCommand. Pure functions with no signal use (e.g. fetchStatus) can stay module-scope. Also refresh the voices list on dialog open via `fetchVoices().then(() => openDialog())` so it's never stale when the service was down at startup.

observations.title: TTS read markdown symbols aloud (fixed)
observations.content:
**What**: TTS engine read raw markdown aloud ("asterisk asterisk", backticks) because auto-read sent assistant text parts verbatim. Added stripMarkdown() applied in chunkText (single funnel for all TTS text: auto-read + custom speak).
**Why**: User reported the voice literally pronounced "**" from formatted responses.
**Where**: src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx — stripMarkdown() called at top of chunkText().
**Learned**: chunkText is the only funnel for TTS text, so stripping there covers both auto-read (lastAssistantText) and the "Speak custom text" dialog. Markdown strip order matters: code blocks -> inline code (keep text) -> images/links -> bold -> strike -> italic -> headings/blockquote/rules/list markers -> html tags. Service/bridge unchanged (text already clean client-side).

observations.title: TTS voice rate + volume controls
observations.content:
**What**: tts-control gained voice speed (0.25–2.0 multipliers) and volume (0–100, step 5) controls across service/bridge/TUI. Both persist in tts-config.json.
**Why**: User requested selectable speed and volume steps in the OpenCode TUI.
**Where**: scripts/tt-service.ps1 (Apply-Rate/Apply-Volume, Speak-Text SSML wrap for rate), src/tts-bridge.ts (/rates,/rate,/volumes,/volume), src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx (rate/volume signals, DialogSelect selectors, label shows ⚡x× and 🔉x%).
**Learned**: SpeechSynthesizer.Rate is only int -10..10, so precise speed REQUIRES SSML <prosody rate="+50.00%"> (multiplier→pct = (m-1)*100). Volume IS int 0..100 directly (synth.Volume). Closure rule: Speak-Text must be script-scope so the SpeakCompleted event handler (registered earlier in file) can call it. Config loads voice/rate/volume on startup.

observations.title: tts-control restart requires killing stale singleton
observations.content:
**What**: tts-control service is a Windows singleton (Global mutex "Global\tts-control-service") launched hidden from C:\Windows\Temp\tt-service.ps1 by start.sh. Relaunching does NOT kill the old instance — the new one sees the mutex taken and exits (line 26), so the OLD code keeps serving on 9876. Bridge (9877) runs in WSL as a bun process and also must be killed or the new bind fails (EADDRINUSE).
**Why**: User reported rate/volume TUI controls had no effect — root cause was a stale running service without those commands, not a code bug.
**Where**: scripts/start.sh and scripts/start-bridge.sh now kill stale listeners first: 9876 via `powershell.exe Get-NetTCPConnection ... Stop-Process` (Windows side), 9877 via `fuser -k 9877/tcp` (WSL side).
**Learned**: Service = Windows process (kill by port via powershell.exe). Bridge = WSL/Linux process (kill via fuser/lsof in bash). For ANY new service/bridge feature to take effect, the running processes must be killed — re-running start.sh now handles this automatically. Config (voice/rate/volume) persists at C:\Windows\Temp\tts-config.json (PSScriptRoot of the temp copy), not in repo.

observations.title: TTS volume ignored on SSML path (rate != 1)
observations.content:
**What**: Speed (rate) control produced NO audio when rate != 1.0, and volume was also ignored on that path. Root cause: the service spoke via SpeakSsmlAsync with SSML <prosody rate=...>. Windows System.Speech IGNORES the SSML <prosody rate> attribute entirely (verified: 200/100/50/25% all rendered at ~same duration) and also requires a valid <speak> (missing xml:lang threw "requiere el atributo lang"). So the SSML path was silently dropped = silence.
**Why**: User reported "cuando le cambio la velocidad no se escucha nada". The plain SpeakAsync path (rate=1.0) worked, masking the bug.
**Where**: scripts/tt-service.ps1 — Speak-Text now uses plain Synth.SpeakAsync with `$synth.Rate = [int]::Round((rate-1)*10)` (mapped from multiplier, clamped -10..10) and `$synth.Volume`. SSML removed entirely.
**Learned**: (1) SSML <prosody rate> is ignored by Windows SpeechSynthesizer — use the Rate int property (-10..10) instead. (2) synth.Volume DOES apply with plain SpeakAsync (the earlier "volume ignored" was only on the SSML path). (3) SSML <speak> needs xml:lang or it throws. DROP SSML for this engine. Multiplier->int mapping is approximate (rate=5 tested ~1.8x), not exact.

observations.title: Session summary: tts-control
observations.content:
## Goal
Make TTS speed (rate) and volume controls actually audible from the OpenCode TUI.

## Instructions
- User speaks Spanish (Rioplatense voseo); reply in Spanish.
- Cannot audio-test from WSL; verify via Windows property set + bridge /status + timed Speak/SpeakSsml in Windows.
- Keep responses short; explain root cause technically when fixing.

## Discoveries
- Windows System.Speech IGNORES the SSML `<prosody rate>` attribute (verified: long phrase at 200/100/50/25% all rendered ~11s — no speed change).
- SSML `<speak>` requires `xml:lang` or it throws "requiere el atributo lang".
- `synth.Rate` (int -10..10) DOES control speed — verified: rate=5 -> 22.86s vs rate=0 -> 41.15s on same long phrase.
- `synth.Volume` DOES apply with plain SpeakAsync (only ignored on the SSML path).
- Service is a singleton (mutex Global\tts-control-service); relaunch does NOT kill the old instance -> must kill stale port 9876 before relaunch.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Fixed rate silence: rewrote Speak-Text to DROP SSML entirely; now plain SpeakAsync with `$synth.Rate = [int]::Round(($script:rate - 1) * 10)` clamped -10..10, and `$synth.Volume = $script:volume`. File: scripts/tt-service.ps1.
- ✅ Volume audibility fixed as a side effect (was only ignored on the now-removed SSML path).
- ✅ Redeployed (copied to C:\Windows\Temp\tt-service.ps1) + restarted service; verified speaks at 1.5x and 0.5x complete (status -> idle).
- ✅ Memories: #655 markdown fix, #656 rate+volume, #657 restart singleton, #658 SSML rate root cause (updated).

## Next Steps
- (none pending) rate + volume both audible from TUI. Optional: refine multiplier -> int Rate mapping if user wants closer-to-exact speeds (current mapping is approximate, e.g. rate=5 measured ~1.8x).

## Relevant Files
- scripts/tt-service.ps1 — Speak-Text (~line 156) now plain SpeakAsync + synth.Rate/synth.Volume; Apply-Rate sets $script:rate only.
- src/tts-bridge.ts — /rate,/rates,/volume,/volumes routes (working, unchanged).
- src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx + ~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/tts-monitor.tsx — TUI selectors + stripMarkdown (deployed).
- scripts/start.sh, start-bridge.sh — kill stale ports 9876/9877 before launch.
- C:\Windows\Temp\tts-config.json — persisted voice/rate/volume.

observations.title: TTS distinct beep tones + sound toggle
observations.content:
**What**: Added category-distinct notification beeps to the TTS monitor. `/beep` (bridge) now accepts `{kind}` → result (two ascending notes 880→1320Hz), error (low descending 330→220), info (soft blip 660), alert (single 880, default). Plugin maps: session.idle WITH readable text → playBeep("result"); session.idle WITHOUT text (abort/error) → playBeep("error"); manual Speak action → playBeep("info"). Added a persisted 🔔/🔕 Sound toggle (api.kv "tts.sound", default true) gating all beeps. Label shows 🔔/🔕.
**Why**: User wanted to distinguish "result notification" from "the others" by sound.
**Where**: src/tts-bridge.ts (BEEP_TONES map + /beep kind param); src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx (playBeep(kind), soundOn signal, session.idle mapping, __sound__ dialog toggle, refreshLabel icon). Deployed copy at ~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/tts-monitor.tsx.
**Learned**: (1) Bridge runs on WSL; `powershell.exe` IS callable from WSL (interop) so `[Console]::Beep` works — but the old `Bun.os !== "windows"` guard wrongly blocked it. Removed guard; rely on try/catch. (2) `Bun.$` ONLY accepts tagged template literals `$`...``; the array-arg form `Bun.$(...)` throws "Please use $ as a tagged template function". Pass dynamic values via `${var}` interpolation so they stay ONE argv token (spaces/; preserved). (3) OpenCode TUI plugin does NOT hot-reload — after editing the deployed .tsx, the user must restart OpenCode/reload the TUI for new plugin code to load. (4) `Bun.os` is undefined in this Bun build (don't rely on it).

observations.title: TTS README + dual-frontend decision (keep both)
observations.content:
**What**: Creé README.md con reinstalación + uso. Decisión: mantener AMBOS frentes sin borrar — plugin OpenCode (tts-monitor.tsx) = canónico/"lo nuevo que funciona"; standalone tts-tui.ts = alternativa documentada. 
**Why**: User: "no borra lo viejo, la idea solo tener lo nuevo que funciona y crea el readme con instrucciones para reinstalar y usar".
**Where**: README.md (nuevo); src/tts-tui.ts (standalone, sin tocar); src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx (canónico).
**Learned**: El standalone tts-tui.ts DIVERGIÓ del plugin: solo tiene pause/stop/toggle, NO rate/volumen/beeps/sound-toggle. README lo marca como alternativa "para usar sin OpenCode". start.sh lanza el standalone en foreground (línea 58) — eso es confuso porque el usuario usa el plugin; README aclara que el camino recomendado es OpenCode + plugin (Alt+U). No se modificó start.sh para no alterar lo viejo.

observations.title: Session summary: tts-control
observations.content:
## Goal
TTS control for OpenCode TUI: voice + speed (rate) + volume + distinct notification sounds, all audible from the TUI, plus a README to reinstall/use.

## Instructions
- User speaks Spanish (Rioplatense voseo); reply in Spanish.
- Cannot audio-test from WSL; verify via Windows property-set + bridge /status + timed Speak in Windows + curl on bridge endpoints.
- Keep old code; the OpenCode plugin is the canonical "new working" path (user: "no borra lo viejo, solo tener lo nuevo que funciona").

## Discoveries
- Windows System.Speech IGNORES the SSML `<prosody rate>` attribute (verified: 200/100/50/25% all rendered ~same duration). SSML `<speak>` also REQUIRES `xml:lang` or it throws.
- `synth.Rate` (int -10..10) DOES control speed; `synth.Volume` (0-100) DOES apply — but ONLY with plain `SpeakAsync`, not on the SSML path.
- Bridge runs on WSL; `powershell.exe` IS callable from WSL (interop) so `[Console]::Beep` works. The old `Bun.os !== "windows"` guard wrongly blocked it (Bun.os is `undefined` here) — removed, rely on try/catch.
- `Bun.$` ONLY accepts tagged template literals `$`...``; the array-arg form `Bun.$(...)` throws "Please use $ as a tagged template function". Pass dynamic values via `${var}` interpolation so they stay ONE argv token.
- OpenCode TUI plugin does NOT hot-reload — after editing the deployed .tsx, the user must restart OpenCode.
- Rate mapping is approximate (Windows speed is stepped int -10..10, not exact multipliers).

## Accomplished
- ✅ Rate silence fixed: rewrote Speak-Text to drop SSML, use plain SpeakAsync with `$synth.Rate = [int]::Round(($script:rate - 1) * 10)` clamped -10..10 + `$synth.Volume`. scripts/tt-service.ps1.
- ✅ Volume audibility fixed as side effect (was only ignored on the now-removed SSML path). Verified speaks at 1.5x and 0.5x complete (idle).
- ✅ Distinct beep tones: bridge `/beep` now accepts `{kind}` → result (two ascending notes), error (low descending), info (soft blip), alert (single). Plugin maps session.idle-with-text → "result", session.idle-without-text (abort/error) → "error", manual Speak → "info". Added persisted 🔔/🔕 Sound toggle (api.kv "tts.sound", default true). src/tts-bridge.ts + src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx.
- ✅ README.md created (Spanish, matches project): prerequisites, reinstall steps, run, usage (Alt+U), caveats, file table. Documents plugin as canonical path; standalone tts-tui.ts as alternative (kept, not deleted).
- ✅ Decision: keep BOTH frontends (plugin + standalone), plugin = canonical. start.sh launches the standalone in foreground (older, lacks rate/volume/beeps) — README clarifies to use OpenCode + plugin.
- ✅ Memories saved: #658 SSML rate root cause, #659/earlier markdown, #660 beep tones+sound toggle, #661 README+dual-frontend decision.

## Next Steps
- (optional) Upgrade `pause` to real mid-speech pause via `$synth.Pause()`/`Resume()` (today it only gates the next chunk).
- (optional) Single combined deploy/run script (deploy.sh only copies the plugin; service .ps1 is copied by start.sh).
- Tick the stale spec checkboxes in context/kits/tts-service.md (features are done, boxes just never checked).

## Relevant Files
- scripts/tt-service.ps1 — Speak-Text (~line 156) plain SpeakAsync + synth.Rate/synth.Volume; stop clears queue + SpeakAsyncCancelAll.

observations.title: Session summary: tts-control
observations.content:
## Goal
TTS control para la TUI de OpenCode: voz + velocidad + volumen + sonidos de notificación distintos, todo audible desde la TUI; README con diagrama; y subir el proyecto a GitHub con licencia MIT.

## Instructions
- User habla español (Rioplatense voseo); responder en español.
- No se puede audio-testear desde WSL; verificar vía seteo de propiedades en Windows + `/status` del bridge + Speak temporizado en Windows + curl a endpoints.
- Mantener código viejo; el plugin de OpenCode es el camino "nuevo que funciona" (user: "no borra lo viejo, solo tener lo nuevo que funciona").
- Commitear TODO el repo (incl. .kiro/, context/, backup/, .atl/); excluir solo lo del .gitignore.

## Discoveries
- Windows System.Speech IGNORA el atributo `<prosody rate>` de SSML (verificado: 200/100/50/25% dan todas ~misma duración). SSML `<speak>` además REQUIERE `xml:lang` o tira. Por eso se DROPEÓ SSML: `synth.Rate` (int -10..10) y `synth.Volume` (0-100) SÍ funcionan, pero solo con `SpeakAsync` plano.
- `Bun.$` SOLO acepta template tag `$`...``; la forma con array `Bun.$(...)` tira "Please use $ as a tagged template function". Pasar valores dinámicos por interpolación `${var}`.
- `Bun.os` es `undefined` en WSL → el guard `Bun.os !== "windows"` bloqueaba los beeps. Se removió; confiar en try/catch.
- El plugin de TUI de OpenCode NO hace hot-reload → tras editar el .tsx hay que reiniciar OpenCode.
- El servicio es singleton (mutex global) → relanzarlo NO mata la instancia vieja; start.sh la mata primero.
- El mapeo de rate es aproximado (la velocidad de Windows es int escalonado -10..10, no multiplicadores exactos).
- `gh` CLI está autenticado como davidcoachdev con scope `repo` → se puede crear repo y pushear sin pedir URL.

## Accomplished
- ✅ Velocidad audible: Speak-Text reescrito a SpeakAsync plano con `$synth.Rate = [int]::Round(($script:rate-1)*10)` clamp -10..10 + `$synth.Volume`. SSML eliminado. scripts/tt-service.ps1.
- ✅ Volumen audible (side-effect del fix anterior; antes solo se ignoraba en el path SSML).
- ✅ Beeps distintos: bridge `/beep?kind=` (result/error/info/alert) + mapa BEEP_TONES; plugin mapea session.idle-con-texto→"result", session.idle-sin-texto→"error", Speak manual→"info". Toggle 🔔/🔕 persistido (api.kv "tts.sound"). Verificados los 4 tonos.
- ✅ README.md (español) con diagrama Mermaid de arquitectura; plugin marcado CANÓNICO.
- ✅ Git init en `main`, commit inicial de TODO el repo (51 archivos). `.gitignore` excluye node_modules/ bin/ dist/ *.log .DS_Store backend/.
- ✅ Repo subido a GitHub (privado) via `gh repo create tts-control --private --source=. --push` → https://github.com/davidcoachdev/tts-control, `main` trackea `origin/main`.
- ✅ Licencia MIT agregada (commit 2bb08f9) y pusheada.
- ✅ Memorias: #658 (root cause SSML rate), #660 (beeps+sound toggle), #661 (README+decisión dual-frontend), #663 (git init + GitHub + MIT license).

## Next Steps
- (opcional) Subir `pause` a pausa real de Windows (`$synth.Pause()`/`Resume()`; hoy solo corta el siguiente chunk).
- (opcional) Script único de deploy+run (deploy.sh solo copia el plugin; el .ps1 lo copia start.sh).
- (opcional) Tickear los checkboxes de spec en context/kits/tts-service.md (las features están, las cajas no).
- (opcional) Hacer el repo PÚBLICO si se desea: `gh repo edit tts-control --visibility public`.

## Relevant Files
- scripts/tt-service.ps1 — Speak-Text (~line 156) SpeakAsync plano + synth.Rate/synth.Volume; stop limpia queue + SpeakAsyncCancelAll.
- src/tts-bridge.ts — /beep?kind= (BEEP_TONES), /rate /volume /voice /speak passthrough a TCP :9876.
- src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx + ~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/tts-monitor.tsx — panel TUI (selectores voz/rate/vol, beeps, toggle sonido, stripMarkdown). Reiniciar OpenCode para recargar.
- src/client.ts (CLI TCP standalone), src/tts-tui.ts (app OpenTUI standalone, vieja/divergida) — alternativas, se mantienen.
- scripts/start.sh (servicio+bridge+app standalone), start-bridge.sh, deploy.sh (copia solo plugin).
- README.md — reinstalación + uso + diagrama Mermaid.
- LICENSE — MIT, Copyright 2026 davidcoachdev.
- C:\Windows\Temp\tts-config.json — voz/rate/vol persistidos.

observations.title: Mid-speech pause must be verified (STA threading risk)
observations.content:
**What**: User flagged caution about implementing real mid-speech pause via $synth.Pause()/Resume() — worried it could break reading mid-utterance.
**Why**: Valid concern. System.Speech SpeechSynthesizer runs on an STA thread; calling Pause/Resume from a different thread (the bridge/HTTP or TCP-handler thread) can DEADLOCK or no-op. Pause() when idle/queue empty may also throw.
**Where**: Future work on scripts/tt-service.ps1 Speak-Text real pause; bridge /pause endpoint. Current pause only gates next chunk (does not pause current audio).
**Learned**: Before coding real pause, VERIFY (don't assert from memory): (a) Pause/Resume invoked on same thread as SpeakAsync via SynchronizationContext/Dispatcher — NOT from bridge thread; (b) guard against Pause when queue empty/idle; (c) test mid-utterance in Windows, not just queue-gating. Service must be restarted to redeploy (.ps1 copied by start.sh). User explicitly wants this checked before implementing.

observations.title: OpenCode running session caches agent config; restart needed after edits
observations.content:
**What**: After editing custom-agents.json and re-merging to opencode.json, spawning cavekit-* subagents STILL used the old (invalid) model until OpenCode was restarted.
**Why**: The running session reads agent/subagent definitions from in-memory cached config, not the freshly-written opencode.json.
**Where**: `merge-custom-agents.sh` prints "Reiniciá OpenCode para que toma los cambios." Confirmed via repeated `task(cavekit-sketch)` failures post-merge.
**Learned**: Any change to agent model/tools/prompt requires an OpenCode restart to affect subagent spawns via the task tool. To run a true multi-agent Cavekit flow after config changes, restart first; otherwise drive phases inline.

observations.title: Fixed TTS Alt+P toggle (pause/resume vs autoRead)
observations.content:
**What**: En tt-service.ps1 el comando TCP `toggle` hacía `-not $S.autoRead` (autoRead toggle) en vez de pausar/reanudar el habla. El plugin manda Alt+P→:tts-toggle→POST /toggle esperando pause/resume, por eso "no funcionaba".
**Why**: El autor del .ps1 implementó `toggle` como auto-lectura, pero el plugin (y client.ts --toggle) lo documentan como pause/resume.
**Where**: scripts/tt-service.ps1 (bloque `if ($cmd -eq "toggle")`), src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx.
**Learned**: `$S.autoRead` del servicio NUNCA se lee en ningún lado (solo se inicializa y se devuelve en status); es safe cambiar `toggle` a pause/resume. El plugin se despliega con scripts/deploy.sh (copia src → ~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/, que es symlink a dcfiles). OpenCode NO recarga el plugin solo: hay que reiniciarlo. El servicio es singleton: hay que relanzarlo (start.sh mata :9876) para que cargue el .ps1 nuevo.

observations.title: OpenCode TUI: usar api.ui.toast, no api.attention.notify, para toasts visibles
observations.content:
**What**: Para mostrar notificaciones VISIBLES dentro de la TUI de OpenCode desde un plugin, usar `api.ui.toast({ variant, title?, message })` (siempre se muestra). `api.attention.notify({...})` se SALTA silenciosamente cuando la app está enfocada (el caso común: el usuario mirando la TUI), por eso "no se ve nada".
**Why**: El plugin tts-monitor usaba api.attention.notify y el usuario reportó "no me muestra las notificaciones". El subagent-statusline plugin (que sí se ve) usa api.ui.toast.
**Where**: tui.d.ts (TuiPluginApi.ui.toast línea ~484; TuiAttention.notify línea ~215). Plugin tts en src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx.
**Learned**: Para campana/sonido usar api.attention.notify con `notification: false` + `sound: { name }` (ej. "subagent_done", "done", "error") como complemento del toast visual, no como reemplazo. OpenCode 1.17.18 / plugin-sdk 1.15.13: api.ui.toast confirmado presente y estable. No confundir: el binario de opencode es compilado (no grepeable), pero el SDK declara el API.

observations.title: TTS nav bindings Alt+,/Alt+. (keymap accepts punctuation)
observations.content:
**What**: Registered `Alt+,` (→`:tts-prev`) and `Alt+.` (→`:tts-next`) TTS paragraph-nav bindings in tts-monitor.tsx; verified the @opentui/keymap keymap does NOT reject punctuation key names.
**Why**: The kit (tts-paragraph-nav) specified a fallback (`Alt+[`/`Alt+]`) "if the keymap rejects comma/period". Investigated `parseStringKeyPart` in `@opentui/keymap/addons` (src/addons/index.js) — it splits on `+`, treats the last non-modifier token as the key `name` with no character-class whitelist, so `","`/`"."` parse fine. Rejection condition is NOT met → primary pair registered, fallback not needed.
**Where**: src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx (keymap layer, priority 100); pure core moved to src/plugins/tts-monitor/nav-logic.ts.
**Learned**: (1) Pure core (splitByParagraph/buildParagraphPieces/navigate/speakParagraphSequentially + moved stripMarkdown/chunkText) is unit-tested via `bun test` (17 pass). (2) `tsc --noEmit` on tts-monitor.tsx is ambientally BLOCKED in this WSL env — missing `@opencode-ai/plugin/tui`, `solid-js`, `@opentui/keymap/addons` module types → only TS2307/TS2347/TS2875 appear, which cascade from missing modules. Real code errors (e.g. async run handlers needing `async`) were fixed; rely on bun test + manual diff review. (3) `CommandResult` accepts `Promise<boolean>`, so command `run` may be `async` and the executor awaits it.

observations.title: Added :tts-help commands panel (Alt+H)
observations.content:
**What**: Added `:tts-help` command + `Alt+h` binding to tts-monitor.tsx. Opens a read-only "🔊 Comandos TTS" panel (showTtsHelp) listing all TTS commands grouped by source (OpenCode plugin Alt+P/U/,/./X/H + standalone app p/s/t/q/c) with keybinding + description and a `[Esc] Volver` hint. Esc closes via api.ui.dialog.clear() (same mechanism as config()).
**Why**: User wanted a visual in the plugin (the "complete version") showing all commands and a way back to the main menu. Earlier misread sent it to standalone tts-tui.ts; that was reverted (git checkout), then correctly built in the plugin.
**Where**: src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx only (mirrors showTtsConfig()/config() close pattern).
**Learned**: When opening help while config dialog is open, dialog.replace supersedes config state (acceptable for modal); double-clear (onClose + box.onKeyDown) is safe because both wrapped in try/catch. h key was unused in the keymap layer.

observations.title: OpenTUI Renderable visible toggle + requestRender
observations.content:
**What**: @opentui/core Renderable has a `visible` boolean getter/setter and renderer has `requestRender()`; show/hide panels by toggling `renderable.visible` rather than add/remove.
**Why**: Needed a second "Commands" view in tts-tui.ts without leaking renderables or breaking the poll loop.
**Where**: src/tts-tui.ts (TtsTui class); node_modules/@opentui/core/Renderable.d.ts (visible:167/169, requestRender on renderer line 388).
**Learned**: Escape key in raw mode arrives as a lone 0x1b byte (data[0]===0x1b, str.length===1), NOT a named string. `bun build --dry-run` fails on opentui's platform-specific dynamic imports (darwin/linux-arm64) — that's ambient, not a syntax error; use `bun build --external "@opentui/*"` for a real syntax check.

observations.title: TTS plugin help panel mirrors config() dialog close
observations.content:
**What**: Added `:tts-help` (Alt+H) read-only command panel to tts-monitor.tsx, mirroring `showTtsConfig()`'s close mechanism.
**Why**: User wanted a help view reusing the exact settings-dialog pattern (BoxRenderable with border/title/flexDirection/padding) and same close path.
**Where**: src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx — `showTtsHelp()` + `:tts-help` command + `Alt+h` binding (priority-100 layer).
**Learned**: In this OpenTUI TUI plugin, a custom modal = `api.ui.dialog.replace(() => <box border title flexDirection padding focusable onKeyDown>, onClose)`. Esc→close is handled two ways that both call `api.ui.dialog.clear()`: (1) the dialog stack's `onClose` 2nd arg, and (2) `onKeyDown={(key)=> key.name==='escape'}` on the focusable box. `KeyEvent.name==="escape"` for Esc. `<text>` bold = nested `<strong>` (not a `bold` prop). Keep `close()` in try/catch so nothing throws. No new deps; dialog API from `@opencode-ai/plugin` (resolved at runtime from ~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/node_modules).

observations.title: OpenCode TUI plugins are single-file (relative imports fail silently)
observations.content:
**What**: OpenCode TUI plugins (loaded via tui.json "plugin" array → .tsx files) are transpiled/loaded as SINGLE FILES. The loader only resolves bare specifiers (@opencode-ai/plugin, solid-js, @opentui/...); it does NOT resolve relative imports like `./nav-logic`.
**Why**: A `import { ... } from "./nav-logic"` in tts-monitor.tsx threw at load time and OpenCode swallowed it SILENTLY — killing the ENTIRE plugin, so even base shortcuts (Alt+P) stopped working. Reverting to base (no relative import) made it load again. Working plugins (engram.ts, rtk.ts, background-agents.ts) only use bare specifiers, never `./`.
**Where**: ~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/tts-monitor.tsx (symlink → ~/Proyects/dcfiles/config/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/tts-monitor.tsx); scripts/deploy.sh.
**Learned**: RULE — never use relative `./` imports across files in an OpenCode TUI plugin. Inline shared logic OR duplicate it in the single file. Keep standalone test copies (nav-logic.ts + nav-logic.test.ts) in the repo for `bun test`, but the deployed .tsx must be self-contained. OpenCode does NOT hot-reload TUI plugins → must restart to see changes.

observations.title: OpenCode TUI dialog: raw <box> won't close on Esc; use DialogSelect
observations.content:
**What**: In an OpenCode TUI plugin, `api.ui.dialog.replace(() => <box ... onKeyDown={esc->clear}>, close)` does NOT close on Esc — the raw `<box>` is not focusable in the dialog stack, so its `onKeyDown` never fires and the dialog stays open ("se traba"). The reliable close mechanism is `api.ui.DialogSelect` with `onCancel={() => api.ui.dialog.clear()}` (and `onSelect`).
**Why**: Built a `:tts-help` panel as a standalone `<box>`; user reported it got stuck and didn't follow the config UI. Fix: make help a SUB-VIEW of the config menu using `DialogSelect` (same proven close path); Esc/Volver calls `api.ui.dialog.clear()` then re-opens `showTtsConfig()`.
**Where**: src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx — showTtsHelp() + the `__help__` option inside showTtsConfig().
**Learned**: For any OpenCode TUI dialog that must be dismissable, use `api.ui.DialogSelect` (or a component that wires Esc to onCancel). Never rely on a raw `<box onKeyDown>` for close. Also: nest sub-views by re-opening the parent after clear (mirrors the toggle pattern in showTtsConfig).

observations.title: OpenCode/OpenTUI: Alt+punctuation doesn't emit; use Alt+letter/Alt+arrow
observations.content:
**What**: In this environment, `Alt+,` / `Alt+.` (Alt + punctuation) do NOT fire keybindings, while `Alt+P` / `Alt+U` / `Alt+X` / `Alt+H` (Alt + letters) DO work. The keymap PARSER accepts punctuation (`@opentui/keymap` parseStringKeyPart accepts any char), but the TERMINAL/OpenTUI input layer never emits a `meta+","` event — `ESC + ","` is read as `Escape` then `","`, so the binding never matches.
**Why**: User reported Alt+,/. "no sirve" while other Alt shortcuts worked. Confirmed OpenTUI natively handles `meta+left`/`meta+right` (and meta+letter) — see @opentui/core index.js:5065-5066 (`name:"left"/"right", meta:true`). Named keys are "left"/"right" (not "arrowleft").
**Where**: src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx — tts-prev/tts-next bindings. Now bound to BOTH "Alt+,"/"Alt+." (harmless if unsupported) AND "Alt+Left"/"Alt+Right" (reliable fallback).
**Learned**: For OpenCode TUI plugin keybindings, prefer Alt+LETTER or Alt+ARROW combos. Avoid Alt+punctuation — it silently won't emit in most terminals. Also: paragraph-nav `paras` model must be populated on-demand (ensureParas) since session.idle only fires it during auto-read; manual nav otherwise no-ops on empty `paras`.

observations.title: OpenCode TUI dialog: onClose cierra en Esc para cualquier nodo
observations.content:
**What**: En plugins TUI de OpenCode, un `<box>` crudo pasado a `api.ui.dialog.replace(render)` SE TRAVA: no recibe el foco ni cierra con Esc (el diálogo NO llama onClose para un box sin foco). El `onClose` 2do parámetro NO cierra un box crudo.
**Why**: Intento de panel de solo-lectura con `<box>` + `onClose` → el diálogo no le da foco al box, Escape no cierra, el usuario queda atrapado ("no se puede hacer nada").
**Where**: src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx — showTtsHelp.
**Learned**: Para CUALQUIER diálogo que deba cerrarse con Esc, usar `api.ui.DialogSelect` (maneja onCancel→cierra solo, probado y no se traba). Un `<box>` crudo SIEMPRE se traba en diálogo. Para una lista de comandos de solo-lectura, replicar el menú de config con DialogSelect (opciones con onSelect→back) — el fondo de selección es el del tema (consistente con el config). No usar box crudo para diálogos. `TuiDialogSelectOption` tiene `disabled?` pero lo deja el texto casi invisible en algunos temas → no usar para legibilidad. `session.idle` = evento que dispara cuando el agente termina y espera input (hook ideal para beep de "pregunta"). OpenCode transpila el .tsx en runtime; validar con `bun build --no-bundle`.

observations.title: Beep silent on WSL2: use SystemSounds not [Console]::Beep
observations.content:
**What**: The TTS bridge /beep endpoint used `[Console]::Beep(...)` which is SILENT in WSL2 / Windows Terminal.
**Why**: The PC-speaker beep is not routed to the user's audio device in that environment, so no sound ever played (and the plugin's catch swallowed the non-error).
**Where**: src/tts-bridge.ts — BEEP_TONES map (called via `powershell.exe -Command`).
**Learned**: For audible beeps on this stack, use `[System.Media.SystemSounds]::Exclamation/Asterisk/Hand/Question.Play()` (routes through the default Windows audio device). Also: OpenCode's `api.attention.notify` sound "subagent_done" was NOT audible for the user, so added a bridge beep (`playBeep("result")`) on auto-read start instead. powershell.exe is reachable from WSL2 via Windows interop, so the call path itself works.

observations.title: Session summary: tts-control
observations.content:
## Goal
Fix the TTS plugin beep not playing (neither on agent question nor on response) and push the fix to the repo.

## Instructions
- User speaks rioplatense Spanish (voseo); respond in Spanish.
- Environment is WSL2; OpenCode has no TUI plugin hot-reload (must restart OpenCode to load plugin changes).
- Bridge runs on WSL2 Linux, TTS service on Windows; `powershell.exe` is reachable via WSL interop.
- Commit/push freely when the user asks ("subí", "hazlo todo").

## Discoveries
- `[Console]::Beep` is SILENT in WSL2 / Windows Terminal (PC speaker not routed to audio) → beeps never audible. Fix: use `[System.Media.SystemSounds]::X.Play()` (Exclamation/Asterisk/Hand/Question), which routes through the default audio device.
- OpenCode's `api.attention.notify` sound "subagent_done" was also inaudible for the user → added a bridge beep (`playBeep("result")`) on auto-read start instead.
- A raw `<box>` node in `api.ui.dialog.replace` traps focus (won't close with Esc) — must use `api.ui.DialogSelect`. The `disabled` option hides text in some themes. (From earlier in this project.)

## Accomplished
- ✅ Root-caused beep silence: bridge used `[Console]::Beep`.
- ✅ Changed `BEEP_TONES` in `src/tts-bridge.ts` to Windows SystemSounds (alert=Exclamation, result=Asterisk, error=Hand, info=Question).
- ✅ Added `playBeep("result")` on auto-read start in `src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx`.
- ✅ Committed `8acc432` "fix: make beep audible via Windows SystemSounds" and pushed to origin/main.
- ✅ Killed old bridge (PID 489), ran `scripts/deploy.sh` (copied new .tsx), relaunched bridge (PID 52193, listening on 9877, connected to TTS TCP 172.20.112.1:9876), verified `/beep` returns `{"ok":true}`.

## Next Steps
- User restarts OpenCode to load the new plugin; verify beep is audible on question + response.
- If still silent: likely Windows system sounds disabled → switch to `Media.SoundPlayer` playing a .wav.
- (Carried over, not started) Package the plugin as an installable/distributable plugin (build step + manifest + publish).

## Relevant Files
- src/tts-bridge.ts — BEEP_TONES now uses SystemSounds (audible on WSL2).
- src/plugins/tts-monitor/tts-monitor.tsx — added `playBeep("result")` on auto-read start.
- scripts/deploy.sh — copies only tts-monitor.tsx to ~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/.
- /tmp/tts-bridge.log — bridge stdout (relaunched instance).

observations.title: dcfiles: add solo acepta archivos; repo conserva tras borrado en disco
observations.content:
**What**: Comportamiento de `dcfiles` (CLI en ~/.local/bin/dcfiles, repo en DCFILES_HOME=/home/dcdebian/Proyects/dcfiles, que es donde apunta el symlink del CLI).
**Why**: Al respaldar un skill nuevo y luego restaurar skills golang borrados del disco, descubrí varias reglas no obvias.
**Where**: ~/.local/bin/dcfiles, /home/dcdebian/Proyects/dcfiles (repo git de dotfiles)
**Learned**:
1. `dcfiles add <path>` usa `[[ -f ]]` → SOLO acepta archivos regulares, NO directorios. Para añadir un skill entero hay que iterar archivo por archivo (bucle `find -type f | dcfiles add`).
2. El CLI no resuelve rutas absolutas tipo /home/... (da "File not found"); usar ruta relativa a $HOME (ej. `.config/opencode/skills/foo/SKILL.md` desde $HOME) o `~/...`.
3. Si borrás archivos del disco (symlinks), `dcfiles status` los marca `D` (staged delete) pero el REPO git los sigue teniendo. `dcfiles sync` conmutea el estado según el disco. Para restaurar en disco sin perder del repo: `git checkout HEAD -- 'config/.config/opencode/skills/golang-*'` (restaura working tree del repo) y luego `dcfiles sync` (el deploy recrea los symlinks en disco). El repo/remote NO pierde los archivos mientras no hagas commit+push de las D.
4. `dcfiles sync` = deploy symlinks + git add -A + commit + push. Auto-pushea TODO el repo (no es selectivo). Revisar `git status --short` antes.
5. NO asumir "consolidación" de skills sin verificar: un skill placeholder (ej. cc-skills-golang) puede estar vacío en el repo (solo SKILL.md) aunque otros individuales se hayan borrado del disco.

observations.title: AGENTS.md global vs project-scoped (OpenCode leak)

**What**: OpenCode carga `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` como config GLOBAL (se aplica a TODOS los proyectos). El contenido específico de un proyecto (ej. plugin TTS de `tts-control`) debe ir en el `AGENTS.md` de la raíz de ese proyecto, NO en el global.
**Why**: En una sesión previa se escribió el contexto del proyecto TTS en el global, haciendo que se inyectara en Trust-Work-Escrow y otros repos, generando confusión.
**Where**: `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` (global, neutro/vacío) vs `/home/dcdebian/Proyects/tts-control/AGENTS.md` (project-scoped).
**Learned**: Al guardar contexto de un proyecto, escribir SIEMPRE al `AGENTS.md` del repo correspondiente. El global debe quedar neutro. Backup de la fuga quedó en `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md.bak.tts-leak`.

observations.title: Dioxus 0.7 soporta Tailwind nativo + dx components
observations.content:
**What**: Dioxus 0.7 tiene soporte nativo de Tailwind CSS: `dx` auto-detecta `tailwind.css` en la raíz, descarga el binario y corre el watcher; se configura con `[tailwind] input/output` en `Dioxus.toml`. Además existe la skill `tailwind-4` (cargada). `dx components add <name>` genera primitivas accesibles (Radix) en `src/components/` + theme CSS en `assets/`.
**Why**: El usuario pidió usar Tailwind y componentes reutilizables en vez de CSS a mano; verifiqué en el repo/docs de Dioxus.
**Where**: release notes 0.7.0-alpha.0 (Automatic Tailwind); ejemplo `examples/10-integrations/tailwind`.
**Learned**: No estaba usando Tailwind (CSS a mano en main.css). El `ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` de `dx serve` es del lado del server, no del código Rust; probablemente dx 0.7.0 + versiones desalineadas. Para adoptar Tailwind hay que alinear dx+dioxus a la misma 0.7.x reciente y reemplazar el hack `asset!`+`document::Link` por el flujo Tailwind nativo. Falta decidir/confirmar con el usuario y ver logs de `dx serve`.

observations.title: Toolchain rust default pasado a stable 1.97.1
observations.content:
**What**: El default toolchain de rust estaba en 1.89.0; lo cambié a `stable` (rustc 1.97.1) con `rustup default stable` para poder instalar dioxus-cli 0.7 (requiere rustc >=1.96).
**Why**: `cargo install dioxus-cli --version 0.7.0` fallaba por `kstring@2.0.4 requires rustc 1.96.0`.
**Where**: toolchain global (rustup).
**Learned**: build-sbf de Solana usa su propio toolchain pinneado, así que cambiar el default stable no afecta la compilación de programas Solana. También hay que `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` para el target actual (1.97) porque antes solo estaba para 1.89.

observations.title: dx/dioxus version pin must match exactly (0.7.9)
observations.content:
**What**: Pinned dioxus to `=0.7.9` in landing/Cargo.toml (was `0.7` which resolved to 0.7.0). Without the exact pin, `dx check`/`dx serve` fails with "dx and dioxus versions are incompatible!" (dx 0.7.9 vs dioxus 0.7.0).
**Why**: dx 0.7.9 requires the matching dioxus 0.7.9; the loose `0.7` range let cargo pick 0.7.0.
**Where**: landing/Cargo.toml
**Learned**: After editing Cargo.toml run `cargo update -p dioxus` so Cargo.lock bumps to 0.7.9, then `dx check` passes. The landing is a Dioxus 0.7 web project (wasm32 target) — use `dx check`/`dx serve`, not plain `cargo check`.

observations.title: Dioxus 0.7: rustc no reconoce .rsx como módulo; dx check da falsos positivos
observations.content:
**What**: En Dioxus 0.7, los componentes deben estar en archivos `.rs` (con macro `rsx!`). rustc/cargo NO resuelven `mod foo;` a `foo.rsx` — `dx serve`/`dx build` fallan con `error[E0583]: file not found for module` pidiendo `foo.rs` o `foo/mod.rs`. El lenguaje RSX se escribe con la macro `rsx!` dentro de `.rs`.
**Why**: rustc solo compila `.rs`; `.rsx` no es una extensión de módulo válida en este build (a diferencia de `.jsx` en React). El soporte `.rsx` de Dioxus es para el translate tool / language server, no para el compilador.
**Where**: landing/ (todo el árbol src). También: `dx check` NO hace un build real de cargo y dio un falso positivo al tener solo `hero.rsx`; validar siempre con `dx build` o `dx serve`.
**Learned**: Para validar de verdad usá `dx build` (one-shot) o `dx serve`, no `dx check`. Convertir `.rsx`→`.rs` arregla el build sin tocar el contenido RSX ni el theming/Tailwind.

observations.title: Dioxus landing router refactor
observations.content:
**What**: Migrated `landing/` (Trust Work Escrow Dioxus 0.7 web app) from a hand-rolled router (`Route` enum + `Signal<Route>` + manual `match`) to the official `dioxus-router` (`#[derive(Routable)]` + `Router::<Route>{}` + `Link to=...`). Also wired Login/Signup/Contact forms to `use_signal` (controlled inputs + `oninput`/`onsubmit` with `log::info!`).
**Why**: Hand-rolled router gave no real URLs (no deep-link/back-button) and `index.html` advertised hreflang routes that didn't exist. Forms collected nothing.
**Where**: `landing/src/route.rs` (Routable enum), `app.rs` (Router), `ui/navbar.rs` (Link), `features/auth/{login,signup}.rs`, `features/contact/contact.rs`. Cargo.toml gained `router` feature + `log` dep.
**Learned**: `dioxus` `router` feature re-exports the router API through `dioxus::prelude` (NOT `dioxus::router::prelude` — that path doesn't exist and fails to compile). Default history may be MemoryHistory; verify URLs update under `dx serve` (web feature usually selects WebHistory). The tailwind.css hex colors were wrongly flagged as invalid — they're all valid 6-digit; no change needed.

observations.title: Dioxus 0.7 requiere div#main como root en index.html
observations.content:
**What**: La landing en blanco se debía a que index.html no tenía `
`. Dioxus 0.7 (web) usa `Config::default()` → `RootName("main")`. Si falta #main, WebsysDom::new crea un `` DESCONECTADO del DOM (`document.create_element("body")`) y monta ahí → pantalla en blanco (logea error en consola: "element '#main' not found. mounting to the body."). **Why**: El index.html personalizado del proyecto tenía `` vacío, eliminando el punto de montaje que la plantilla oficial de Dioxus sí incluye. **Where**: landing/index.html (body). Confirmado en código fuente dioxus v0.7.0 packages/web/src/cfg.rs (default root "main") y dom.rs (fallback crea body suelto). **Learned**: Siempre incluir `
` dentro de `` en index.html de apps Dioxus web. El uso de `document::Link { rel:"stylesheet", href: MAIN_CSS }` con `asset!("/assets/tailwind.css")` y `dioxus::launch(App)` SÍ es correcto y no era el problema.

observations.title: dioxus-router 0.7: Link requiere contexto de Router (usar layout + Outlet)
observations.content:
**What**: Panic en runtime "`Link` must have access to a parent router" (dioxus-router-0.7.9 link.rs:159) cuando un componente con `Link` se renderiza fuera del `Router`. En la landing, `Navbar` (con `Link`) estaba como hermano de `Router` en app.rs.
**Why**: `Link` solo funciona como descendiente de `Router`; si no, en debug hace panic. El fix correcto en 0.7 es convertir el navbar en un layout: `#[layout(Navbar)]` en el enum `Route` + que `Navbar` renderice `Outlet::<Route> {}` para el contenido de la ruta, y quitar el `Navbar {}`/`main{Router}` explícito de `App` (dejar solo `Router::<Route> {}`).
**Where**: landing/src/route.rs (agregar `use crate::ui::Navbar;` y `#[layout(Navbar)]` antes de la primera ruta), landing/src/ui/navbar.rs (render `main { Outlet::<Route> {} }` al final), landing/src/app.rs (solo `Router::<Route> {}`).
**Learned**: En 0.7 `#[layout(Navbar)]` envuelve TODAS las rutas siguientes hasta el cierre del enum; NO usar `#[end_layout]` al final (causa error de parseo "expected identifier, found }"). El componente layout NO recibe `children`; usa `Outlet::<Route> {}`. Verificado con `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

observations.title: dioxus 0.7.9 dev hot-reload panic (hotreload_utils) - usar --hot-reload false
observations.content:
**What**: Al correr `dx serve` (modo dev) la landing hace panic en wasm: `dioxus-core-0.7.9/src/hotreload_utils.rs:287: index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2` seguido de `RefCell already borrowed`. Es un bug INTERNO del hot-reload de Dioxus 0.7.9, NO del código de la app.
**Why**: En modo dev dx serve envía los templates iniciales vía el protocolo de hot reload; el motor interno (hotreload_utils.rs render_dynamic_node/render_attribute) indexa un pool de nodos dinámicos fuera de rango y panic. El código de hot reload solo se ejecuta con hot reload habilitado.
**Where**: Cualquier app Dioxus 0.7.9 web servida con `dx serve` (hot reload on). No depende de un archivo concreto de la landing.
**Learned**: WORKAROUND confiable: correr `dx serve --hot-reload false` (desactiva hot reload, la app renderiza normal). Alternativa: `dx build --release` + servir la carpeta `dist/` con un static server. No es un bug del usuario; no hace falta cambiar el código para que se vea. Si se quiere live reload, investigar posible trigger (document::Link en root, layout/Outlet) o upgrade de parche dioxus, pero no verificado.

observations.title: Header: Language Switcher y Theme Switcher como componentes separados (ui-kit Excalidraw)
observations.content:
**What**: El header de la landing usa DOS componentes separados (`Language Switcher` y `Theme Switcher`) según el ui-kit Excalidraw. Implementados en `landing/src/ui/language_switcher.rs` y `theme_switcher.rs`, usados en `navbar.rs`.
**Why**: El usuario pidió separarlos y matchear el diseño. El diseño: pills 36x36 (`rounded-full`, border `--border`, bg `--surface`); Language muestra código ("ES"/"EN"); Theme muestra swatch (primary 16x16 + primary-2 8x8).
**Where**: landing/src/ui/language_switcher.rs, theme_switcher.rs, mod.rs, navbar.rs. theme.rs tiene `Theme::swatch_primary()/swatch_secondary()` con los hex por tema (dcdev #ff3c3c/#781414, cyan #00d4ff/#6464c8, solana #14f195/#9945ff) para el preview en el dropdown.
**Learned**: NO usar `<select>` nativo: el popup no se puede tematizar (el usuario reportó "los select no tiene color del tema"). En su lugar son dropdowns propios (popover): `div.relative` + botón pill + al abrir, backdrop `fixed inset-0 z-40` (click cierra) + menú `absolute right-0 mt-2 z-50 min-w-[..] rounded-xl border-border bg-surface text-fg shadow-lg`, cada opción con su swatch (inline style con hex por tema) y check `text-primary` si activa. `Signal::set` requiere binding `mut` y en `for x in X::all()` el item es `&X` (usar `*x`). Para ver landing: `dx serve --hot-reload false`.

observations.content:
## Goal
Arreglar y mejorar la landing page de Trust Work Escrow (Dioxus 0.7.9, web) que no mostraba nada al correrse, y luego pulir el header (componentes del ui-kit Excalidraw) y agregar animaciones (switchers, scroll-reveal de secciones, scrollbar tematizada).

## Instructions
- El usuario corre la landing con dx serve --hot-reload false (el hot reload de dioxus 0.7.9 hace panic en wasm, ver memoria).
- Trabajar en espanol. Confirmar cambios con cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown (compila limpio).
- El diseno de componentes vive en design/themes/<skin>/ui-kit/trust-work-ui-kit-dark.excalidrawlib.

## Discoveries
- Dioxus 0.7 monta en #main por defecto (Config::default RootName main). Sin ese div, crea un body suelto y la pagina queda en blanco.
- Link de dioxus-router requiere contexto de Router; solucion: #layout(Navbar) + Outlet::<Route>. Quitar #end_layout al final del enum (parse error).
- dx serve dev (hot reload on) panic en hotreload_utils.rs en wasm: bug interno de dioxus 0.7.9, no del codigo. Workaround: --hot-reload false.
- animation-timeline: view() solo funciona en Chrome/Edge; en Firefox/Safari no anima nada. Solucion robusta: IntersectionObserver via document::eval (JS) que togglea clase is-visible.
- MountedEvent::inner() es privado; se evito usando document::eval en vez de acceder al DOM desde Rust.

## Accomplished
- index.html: agregado div id=main en el body.
- route.rs: Route usa #[layout(Navbar)] (sin #end_layout).
- app.rs: solo Router::<Route> {} (Navbar ahora es layout).
- navbar.rs: usa LanguageSwitcher y ThemeSwitcher (ya no selects inline).
- Creados src/ui/language_switcher.rs y theme_switcher.rs: pills 36x36 del ui-kit con dropdown propio tematizado (no select nativo, porque el popup no se puede tematizar). theme.rs tiene Theme::swatch_primary/secondary con hex por tema.
- tailwind.css: keyframes dropdown-in/fade-in, scrollbar tematizada con vars del tema, y .reveal con transicion por clase is-visible.
- Creado src/ui/reveal.rs (wrapper div.reveal) y LandingPage envuelve las 7 secciones; IntersectionObserver global en REVEAL_SCRIPT (document::eval) agrega is-visible al hacer scroll.
- Cargo.toml sin deps extra (no hizo falta wasm-bindgen/js-sys). Todo compila.

## Next Steps
- El usuario podria querer stagger de tarjetas internas por seccion, o effects distintos.
- Opcional: investigar trigger del hot-reload panic para recuperar live reload (document::Link o layout/Outlet), o subir parche de dioxus.
- Si al recargar no se ven las animaciones de scroll, verificar que dx serve recompilo tailwind.css (reiniciar server).

## Relevant Files
- landing/index.html (div#main)
- landing/src/route.rs (layout Navbar)
- landing/src/app.rs (Router unico)
- landing/src/ui/navbar.rs, language_switcher.rs, theme_switcher.rs, reveal.rs, mod.rs
- landing/src/theme/mod.rs (swatch methods)
- landing/src/features/landing/mod.rs (IntersectionObserver via eval)
- landing/tailwind.css (keyframes, scrollbar, .reveal)

observations.title: Installed open-code-review (OCR) plugin + CLI for OpenCode
observations.content:
**What**: Installed Alibaba OpenCodeReview CLI + OpenCode plugin; configured for delegation mode so the review runs on OpenCode's own model (hy3), no external LLM key.
**Why**: Pilot OCR as a precision-focused first-pass reviewer integrated into OpenCode. User has no external LLM key (no anthropic/opus), so delegation is the only viable path.
**Where**: Plugin ~/.config/opencode/plugins/open-code-review.ts (global, loads after OpenCode restart); CLI `ocr` v1.7.17; config ~/.opencodereview/config.json (provider=anthropic, model=claude-opus-4-6, api_key unset → irrelevant for delegation).
**Learned**:
- OCR has NO `opencode` provider; `opencode/hy3` is OpenCode's hosted inference, not a standard API endpoint OCR can call. So `ocr review` (plugin's `/ocr-review`) cannot work without an external key.
- Active path = delegation: `ocr delegate preview [--from main --to branch]` lists reviewable files; `ocr delegate rule <files>` outputs resolved rules. Then the host agent (hy3) performs the line-level review. Zero extra key.
- OCR excludes test files by default (default_path).
**Status (2026-07-27)**: VALIDATED end-to-end on a throwaway TS test repo — plugin loads, OCR does file-selection + rule resolution deterministically, hy3 performs the review correctly. Plugin + our engine confirmed working. (No code findings saved; that test repo review was discarded.)
**Next step**: On a real PR, run `ocr delegate preview --from main --to <branch>` + `ocr delegate rule <files>`, then review with hy3. For automated `/ocr-review` (plugin) later, supply ANTHROPIC/OPENAI/DASHSCOPE_API_KEY in the OpenCode env.

observations.title: Trust-Work-Escrow v3 project context
observations.content:
**What**: v3 is a from-scratch rewrite of a Solana/Anchor escrow protocol (Trust Work Escrow), built in `trust-escrow-v3/` (sibling of v1 `trust-escrow` and v2 `trust-escrow-v2`).
**Why**: v1 worked but was basic; v2 added features but regressed security (broken PDA payouts, wrong fee routing/base, stuck funds). v3 ports function-by-function keeping what was correct and fixing bugs.
**Where**: `/home/dcdebian/Proyects/Trust-Work-Escrow/trust-escrow-v3/` — Anchor 0.30, Rust toolchain 1.85.0, single-file `programs/trust-escrow-v3/src/lib.rs`. declare_id is a placeholder (run `anchor keys sync` before deploy).
**Learned**: Docs are split into `docs/contract/` (code-level) and `docs/scenarios/` (product flows). Both use per-part .md + mermaid.

observations.title: v3 fee model: platform commission + arbitration 5%
observations.content:
**What**: Two separate fees.
1) Platform commission: `fee_bps` (basis points, 0-10000) charged on EVERY successful job; goes to `treasury`. Computed once at `create_job` via `compute_fee(amount, fee_bps)` with checked math, stored as `fee_amount`.
2) Arbitration fee: 2.5% of `job.amount` per party = 5% TOTAL, charged ONLY if a dispute is opened. Goes to the resolver (neutral arbitrator on mutual arbitration, or platform advisor otherwise).
**Why**: v2 bug divided `amount*fee_percent/10000` but validated 0-100, charging ~100x less. v3 uses basis points + `compute_fee` helper. Arbitration fee is distinct from platform commission and only triggers on dispute.
**Where**: `lib.rs` constants `BASIS_POINTS=10000`, `ARBITER_FEE_BPS_PER_PARTY=250`; helper `compute_fee`; `Config.fee_bps`.
**Learned**: If a dispute is opened, BOTH parties pay their 2.5% "les guste o no" (user rule). Without an opened dispute (normal approve, auto-approve by grace) arbitration = $0.

observations.title: v3 arbitration & dispute flow (bonds, advisor)
observations.content:
**What**: Arbitrator is NEUTRAL, assigned by platform (`config.authority`) ONLY when a dispute is opened — never at job creation (avoids ghost jobs + charging for unused service). Dispute opening is two-step async with double signature: `raise_dispute` (party A signs, posts 2.5% bond to `ArbitrationEscrow`) then `accept_dispute` (party B signs, posts 2.5% bond). Both bonds guarantee the loser pays even if awarded 0%.
Resolver gets the 5%: arbitrator (mutual) or `config.advisor` (if one party refuses / arbitrator fails / client vanishes). `advisor` is SEPARATE from `authority`.
`request_platform_intervention` (either party) + `resolve_platform_case` (advisor signer) handles non-mutual cases. Advisor is FREE only for administration WITHOUT an opened dispute.
**Why**: User ruled that opening a dispute always incurs the fee regardless of outcome or who resolves; bonds posted upfront prevent a party escaping payment.
**Where**: designs in `docs/contract/06-disputes.md`, `docs/contract/01-overview.md`, `docs/escenarios/03-04`. `Config.advisor` added to struct + `initialize_config`.
**Learned**: Auto-approve after `SUBMITTED_GRACE` (deterministic, no human bias) is the fair no-complaint option when client is inactive post-delivery.

observations.title: v3 PDA payout pattern: new_with_signer
observations.content:
**What**: Any lamport transfer OUT of a PDA (e.g. `job` PDA paying freelancer/treasury/arbiter) MUST use `CpiContext::new_with_signer` with the PDA's seeds + bump. Transfers INTO a PDA from a signer use plain `CpiContext::new`.
**Why**: v2 used `CpiContext::new` for job-PDA outflows → system program transfer failed at runtime ("missing required signature") because a PDA cannot sign without its seeds. v1 bypassed this with raw `**lamports.borrow_mut()` (fragile). v3 uses new_with_signer (clean + safe).
**Where**: apply in `approve_work`, `cancel_job`, `finalize_dispute_payouts`, `approve_milestone` (all pay from `job` PDA).
**Learned**: Job PDA seeds = `[b"job", client.key().as_ref(), &job_id.to_le_bytes()]`.

observations.title: v1/v2 audit findings fixed in v3
observations.content:
**What**: Key bugs found auditing v1/v2, all fixed in v3:
- v2: job-PDA outflows used `CpiContext::new` (no signer) → runtime fail.
- v2: fee computed `/10000` but validated 0-100 → ~100x undercharge.
- v2: `approve_work` sent fee to PDA `config` instead of `treasury`; `withdraw_treasury` had `treasury` as non-signer SystemAccount + no constraint to config.treasury → broken + wrong routing.
- v2: dispute payouts never collected fee and never closed `job`/`dispute` PDAs → stuck funds + locked rent.
- v2: team-as-freelancer deadlock (PDA can't sign `submit_work`).
- v2: `submit_milestone` blocked submission after deadline; milestones sum not validated vs `amount`.
- v1: double fee (client + freelancer each charged) and raw `lamports.borrow_mut()` manipulation + `.unwrap()` on `job.freelancer`.
**Why**: compiled during security audit before v3 rewrite.
**Learned**: v3 uses single platform fee (client deposit side) + arbitration 5% only on dispute; fees always routed to `treasury` (for platform) / resolver (for arbitration); PDAs always closed to return rent.

observations.title: v3 documentation convention (per-part md + mermaid)
observations.content:
**What**: Every contract part and every product scenario gets its own .md. `docs/contract/` = code-level (README index + 01-overview, 02-errores EN→ES, 03-estado, 04-config, 05-jobs, 06-disputes, 07-milestones, 08-arbiter-pool). `docs/scenarios/` = product flows (README, actores.md + 6 scenario md's). Each .md explains quÉ hace / por quÉ (with audit fixes cited) and uses mermaid diagrams.
**Why**: user wants exhaustive, navigable documentation; each new function/account gets a new md (or updates its part md).
**Where**: `trust-escrow-v3/docs/`.
**Learned**: Error messages documented as EN message + ES translation table (on-chain msg stays English; ES is for docs/UI).

observations.title: v3 implementación completa y compila (todas las instrucciones)
observations.content:
**What**: trust-escrow-v3 está 100% implementado y compila con `anchor build` (IDL generado en target/idl/escrow.json, declare_id sincronizado a J1c4QsjbV9bFEPrFQZZGe8GrGWFxNhtAhhrxJFK2xc1h).
**Why**: se portó función a función desde v1/v2 corrigiendo bugs de auditoría.
**Where**: `trust-escrow-v3/programs/trust-escrow-v3/src/lib.rs`.
**Learned**: Módulos completos: Config (initialize_config, pause, unpause, update_treasury, withdraw_treasury, + advisor), Jobs (create_job, deposit_funds, accept_job, submit_work, approve_work, reject_work, cancel_job), ArbiterPool (create/add/remove), Disputes (raise_dispute, accept_dispute, submit_evidence, assign_arbiter, resolve_dispute, resolve_platform_case, request_platform_intervention, finalize_dispute_payouts), Milestones (create/submit/approve/reject). `Config` tiene `authority`, `advisor` (separado), `treasury`, `fee_bps`, `paused`, `bump`. Fee plataforma via compute_fee(basis points); arbitraje 2.5% c/u (bonos en ArbitrationEscrow), resolutor cobra 5%. Pagos PDA con new_with_signer; PDAs siempre se cierran. Milestones pagan su monto y el release final paga el resto. Pendiente: tests/IDL/doc deploy (fase 04 original).

observations.title: v3 build/IDL: usar anchor build, no cargo --features idl-build
observations.content:
**What**: Para generar el build + IDL de v3, usar `anchor build` (Anchor CLI 0.32.1 disponible) desde la raíz de trust-escrow-v3. `cargo build --features idl-build` FALLA con "Safety checks failed: Failed to get program path" porque el safety check de idl-build necesita la ruta de programa que solo provee `anchor build`. `cargo check --lib` / `cargo build` (sin idl-build) sí compilan la librería.
**Why**: el `#[program]` con feature idl-build paniquea fuera del entorno anchor.
**Where**: trust-escrow-v3/. Después de `anchor build`, correr `anchor keys sync` para fijar declare_id (reemplaza el placeholder) y rebuild.
**Learned**: anchor build tarda similar a cargo en compilaciones cached; la primera vez baja muchas deps (anchor-lang-idl, spl-token, etc.).

observations.title: Plan: OpenCode tool + skill para OCR de PDF/imagen (Unlimited-OCR)
observations.content:
**What**: Diseño acordado (pendiente de construir) para un tool + skill de OpenCode que extraiga texto/Markdown desde PDF o imagen, usando baidu/Unlimited-OCR como modelo backend.

**Why**: El usuario quiere una capacidad de "sacar info de un PDF o imagen" dentro del flow de OpenCode. Se evaluó el repo baidu/Unlimited-OCR (21.1k stars, MIT, VLM de document-parsing tipo DeepSeek-OCR) y se decidió NO atarse al modelo self-host directo.

**Where** (a crear):
- `plugins/ocr-extract.js` — tool `ocr_extract`: recibe path PDF/imagen → si PDF rasteriza a PNG (pymupdf/pdftoppm) → base64 → POST a endpoint OpenAI-compatible (/v1/chat/completions) → limpia markers `<|det|>...<|/det|>` (funcion remove_det del README) → devuelve Markdown. Endpoint configurable por env var (ej OCR_ENDPOINT).
- `skills/pdf-ocr-extract/SKILL.md` — trigger: "extraer texto de PDF/imagen", "OCR", "parsear documento". Instruye cuándo usar el tool, cómo llamarlo y el post-proceso. Sin lógica de GPU.

**Arquitectura clave**: tool backend-agnostic = cliente delgado contra endpoint OpenAI-compatible. Unlimited-OCR se sirve así vía vLLM o SGLang (SGLang: `python -m sglang.launch_server --model baidu/Unlimited-OCR --port 10000`). Params importantes: ngram_size=35, ngram_window=128 (single/gundam) o 1024 (multi/base), max_length=32768, image_mode gundam|base. infer.py del repo levanta SGLang y manda requests concurrentes.

**Learned / Bloqueante pendiente**: Unlimited-OCR requiere GPU NVIDIA + CUDA (bf16), no corre razonable en CPU. Antes de construir hay que decidir el backend (DECISIÓN PENDIENTE DEL USUARIO):
- A. Self-host SGLang/vLLM local (necesita GPU propia) — ideal si hay GPU.
- B. Baidu Cloud API (de pago, docs en chino) — si no hay GPU.
- C. HF Space gradio_client (gratis pero rate-limit/inestable) — solo pruebas.
El tool se construye igual (agnóstico), pero falta que el usuario confirme si tiene GPU o va remoto para setear default y probar end-to-end.

observations.title: v3 arbitraje: fee a cuenta separada de empresa (no al resolver)
observations.content:
**What**: En trust-escrow-v3, la fee de arbitraje (5% de lo disputado) ya NO va al wallet del resolver (asesor/árbitro). Se creó `Config.arbitration_treasury` (cuenta SEPARADA de `treasury` de protocolo). En `finalize_dispute_payouts` el `ArbitrationEscrow` cierra hacia `arbitration_treasury` y el `shortfall` (bono no posteado recuperado del PDA job) se transfiere ahí. El `resolver` solo firma. Hay `update_arbitration_treasury` y `withdraw_arbitration` paralelos a los de treasury.
**Why**: El usuario exigió contabilidad separada: la fee de arbitraje es ingreso de la empresa, no pago personal del asesor/árbitro.
**Where**: trust-escrow-v3/programs/trust-escrow-v3/src/lib.rs (Config, finalize_dispute_payouts, nuevas instrucciones); docs 04-config, 06-disputes, 09-auditoria #13.
**Learned**: Con este cambio, en arbitraje mutuo el árbitro externo ya NO cobra on-chain; la empresa retiene el 5% en arbitration_treasury y compensa al árbitro OFF-CHAIN. Si algún día se quiere pagar al árbitro on-chain, hay que ajustar el routing (separar su parte de la de la empresa).

observations.title: v3 escrow: tests exist but not runnable in this sandbox (surfpool simnet, no test-validator)
observations.content:
In trust-escrow-v3 there is tests/escrow.ts (mocha/ts-mocha suite) and package.json aligned to @coral-xyz/anchor 0.32.1 + @solana/web3.js. But the integration tests CANNOT run in THIS sandbox.

Environment constraints learned:
- This sandbox only has surfpool on 127.0.0.1:8899, which is a Simnet/simulator (its --help says "Start Simnet"). It cannot deploy custom programs: solana program deploy / anchor deploy HANG (timeout). So integration tests do not run there.
- solana-test-validator is NOT installed (command not found), so anchor test cannot start its own validator.
- Port 18488 the user mentioned is NOT a Solana RPC (returns 404 on root); it seems to be surfpool's web/dashboard, not the JSON-RPC endpoint.

How to run elsewhere: on a machine with a real solana-test-validator, run anchor test (starts validator on 8899). If surfpool occupies 8899, pkill -f surfpool first, or use solana-test-validator --rpc-port 8898 ... & plus anchor test --skip-local-validator with ANCHOR_PROVIDER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8898.

Decision: do not spend time trying to run anchor test in this sandbox; keep surfpool up and commit the tests so the user runs them in their own environment. Also: Anchor /// CHECK: comments are MANDATORY (build fails without them) - do not remove them even if asked to "remove comments".

observations.title: TokenRouter provider config for OpenCode
observations.content:
**What**: TokenRouter configured as OpenAI-compatible custom provider in OpenCode opencode.json
**Why**: User wanted provider added for intelligent AI model routing
**Where**: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json → provider.tokenrouter; ~/.config/opencode/.env (TOKENROUTER_API_KEY); wrapper ~/.local/bin/opencode-tr
**Learned**: CRITICAL: API base URL is `https://api.tokenrouter.com/v1` (NOT .io). TokenRouter API keys start with `sk-` (NOT tr_ — that was wrong; user's key is sk-EVbK...). OpenCode uses `{env:VAR_NAME}` syntax and does NOT auto-load .env, so wrapper script (opencode-tr) sources .env before launching. Verified: token IS sent (API returns "no access to model", not "Token not provided"). "Token not provided" = user ran `opencode` without wrapper. "no access to model" = TokenRouter account/token lacks model access (needs balance/setup at tokenrouter.com console).

observations.title: Revisión Lightpanda vs Obscura para flow OpenCode
observations.content:
**What**: Analicé el repo lightpanda-io/browser y comparé con Obscura (skill obscura-browser).

**Why**: El usuario pidió evaluar si Lightpanda encaja en nuestro flow de codificación con OpenCode y cuál es la diferencia con Obscura.

observations.title: opencode TUI plugin API constraints (text nesting, quota style, clickable)
observations.content: **What**: Built/fixed TUI plugins at `~/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/`: `context-mode-stats.tsx` and `headroom-stats.tsx`. Both register ONLY the `sidebar_content` slot (right panel) so they don't collide with the tts plugin (which uses `session_prompt_right`/`home_prompt_right`). **Why**: Original context-mode plugin crashed with `TextNodeRenderable only accepts strings...` and showed `—` (regex mismatch on `context-mode statusline` output). Headroom plugin mirrors it for `headroom memory stats` + `headroom doctor`. **Where**: `/home/dcdebian/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/{context-mode-stats,headroom-stats}.tsx`; registered in `/home/dcdebian/.config/opencode/tui.json` plugin array (absolute paths). **Learned**: - Solid JSX (`@opentui/solid`) `` children MUST be strings/TextNodeRenderable/StyledText — never a JSX ``. Use `` for sibling ``. Bold via ``, not a `bold` prop. Quota style: `` → `Title` + lines `theme.textMuted`/`theme.success` with `wrapMode="none"`. - Clickable collapse: `` toggling an `expanded` signal; chevron `▸`/`▾` BEFORE the name, active dot `●`/`○` after. - `context-mode statusline` real output: `context-mode ● 67.5 KB kept out · 67.5 KB/day · preserved...`; parse `/([\d.]+ ?[KMG]?B)\s+kept out/i` and `/...\/day/i`. - **headroom gotcha**: `headroom doctor` exits NON-ZERO (status 2) whenever any check fails, so `execSync` THROWS. Capture its output from `e.stdout` in the catch, don't let it crash. Parse proxy state with `/proxy\s*│\s*✓/`; savings with `/savings[^\n]*?(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*%/` (fallback "—" on "no savings"). `headroom memory stats` is always available (Database Size, Total Memories).

observations.title: TTS service hangs - fix by killing stale pwsh + relaunch
observations.content:
**What**: El servicio TTS (tts-control) deja de funcionar porque el proceso pwsh de tt-service.ps1 se cuelga (mutex Global\tts-control-service tomado, conexiones en CLOSE_WAIT) y la instancia nueva tarda 15-30s en inicializar SpeechSynthesizer en frío.
**Why**: El servicio es singleton (mutex global); si la instancia muere mal o se queda hung, el puerto 9876 queda tomado y los relanzamientos salen al instante ("Ya hay una instancia... Saliendo"). El bridge (PID 982, :9877) sigue vivo pero reporta "service offline" tras 60s de timeout.
**Where**: /home/dcdebian/Proyects/tts-control/ (scripts/tt-service.ps1 en Windows, src/tts-bridge.ts en WSL). Puerto servicio TCP :9876 (Windows, escucha en 0.0.0.0), bridge HTTP :9877 (WSL, 127.0.0.1).
**Learned**: Para arreglar SIN reiniciar el bridge/sesión: (1) powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "Stop-Process -Id <PID_colgado> -Force" (encontrar el PID con Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 9876 / Get-Process powershell); (2) relanzar con Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden -FilePath powershell.exe -ArgumentList '-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Windows\Temp\tt-service.ps1'; (3) ESPERAR 15-30s a que aparezca el listener (Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 9876 -State Listen) antes de concluir que falló. Verificar con curl-equivalent: fetch http://127.0.0.1:9877/status debe dar 200. No es firewall (las conexiones sí llegan). powershell.exe interop funciona desde WSL. No matar el bridge (PID 982) salvo que se quiera reiniciar todo vía scripts/start.sh.

observations.title: v3 bug: pagos transfer from job PDA (data) fallan
observations.content:
**What**: En trust-escrow-v3, TODOS los pagos salen del PDA `job` (que guarda los fondos y lleva data del estado) usando `system_program::transfer { from: job, ... }`. El System Program rechaza transferir desde una cuenta con `data.len() > 0` → error "Transfer: `from` must not carry data".
**Why**: El PDA `job` es program-owned y tiene data; el System Program exige `from.data_len() == 0`. Afecta: cancel_job (L678), expire_paused_job (L744), approve_work (L613/625 x2), resolve_support_ticket refund (L1153), finalize_dispute_payouts (payouts desde job).
**Where**: programs/trust-escrow-v3/src/lib.rs (transfers from job en L616,628,682,748,1156 + finalize).
**Learned**: Dos fixes posibles: (A) mínimo = reemplazar `system_program::transfer from job` por manipulación directa de lamports (`**job.try_borrow_mut_lamports()? -= x; **to.try_borrow_mut_lamports()? += x`), válido porque `job` es program-owned; dejar el saldo de rent (no drenar todo) para que el PDA no muera. (B) idiomático = vault PDA aparte (0 data) que guarde los fondos y de ahí se pague. El deposit sigue client→job (wallet→pda, OK). Tests actuales fallan además por cuentas faltantes en el test: createMilestone no pasa `milestone`, raiseDispute no pasa `ticket` (Option PDA), openSupportTicket pasa `dispute` inexistente.

observations.title: Scoped v3 escrow check found blocking gaps
observations.content:
**What**: Reviewed only the recent trust-escrow-v3 Make changes in lib.rs and tests/escrow.ts; no files changed.

Blocking gaps: Dispute::INIT_SPACE reserves about 22,058 bytes due 10x 2,048-byte evidence, exceeding Solana/Anchor 10,240-byte init limit at RaiseDispute line 1574, so raise_dispute is not deployable/useable as written. tests/escrow.ts line 59 silently catches initializeConfig failure; with persistent Surfpool Config, generated advisor may not match stored config.advisor at lib.rs lines 964/1055. resolve_support_ticket refunds full amount+fee (lib.rs 1072-1080) even after approved milestones, rather than remaining unfunded amount. observations.title: Session summary: trust-work-escrow
observations.content:
## Goal
Revisar únicamente la implementación reciente de trust-escrow-v3 hecha por Make, sin modificar archivos ni hacer commits.

observations.title: Surface persistent Config advisor mismatch
observations.content:
**What**: Replaced the silent `initializeConfig` catch with Config fetch/reuse, authority/ advisor validation, treasury reuse, explicit errors, and a retrying Surfpool airdrop helper.

**Where**: `trust-escrow-v3/tests/escrow.ts`

observations.title: Session summary: trust-work-escrow
observations.content:
## Goal
Continuar Make de `trust-escrow-v3` con los tres gaps P1 del Check, sin auditoría general ni commit.

## Instructions
- Responder en español.
- Modificar solo dentro de `trust-escrow-v3/`.
- No hacer commit.
- No emitir Verdict; el Check posterior lo hará.
- Mantener Surfpool en `http://127.0.0.1:8899` sin matarlo.

## Discoveries
- Docs `docs/contract/03-estado.md` y `06-disputes.md` fijan `MAX_DISPUTE_EVIDENCE = 2048` por evidencia y el modelo inline `Dispute.evidence: Vec<Evidence>`, pero no fijan explícitamente un máximo funcional de 10 evidencias ni una arquitectura de PDAs por evidencia. Historial (`f0cdeed`, `512767e`, `aa06a55`) tampoco resuelve esa elección; gap 1 requiere aclaración HITL.
- Config persistente en Surfpool existe, authority coincide con la wallet local, pero su advisor es un pubkey de una ejecución anterior y no hay secret key en el repositorio. Reutilizarlo necesita `TRUST_ESCROW_V3_ADVISOR_KEYPAIR`; sin ella el setup debe fallar claramente.
- `anchor build` pasa tras el fix, con warnings de versiones/configuración preexistentes. `anchor deploy --provider.cluster localnet` falla porque el buffer existente de Surfpool es menor que el tamaño mínimo requerido (`597677 < 600373`), sin matar Surfpool.
- La suite fue bloqueada por estado/infra de Surfpool: primero airdrop interno 429/limit reached; después el setup persistente no puede completar sin signer del advisor. No se debe confundir con fallo del contrato.

## Accomplished
- ✅ En `lib.rs`, `resolve_support_ticket` ahora calcula `remaining_principal = amount - milestones_amount_total` y reembolsa `remaining_principal + fee_amount`; el helper existente valida fondos y conserva rent.
- ✅ En `tests/escrow.ts`, se agregó escenario TDD de ticket posterior a milestone aprobado, esperando principal restante + fee no devengada.
- ✅ Eliminado `catch (_) {}` silencioso; setup intenta leer/reusar Config, valida authority/advisor, reutiliza treasury/arbitration treasury, inicializa solo si no existe y reporta errores explícitos. Airdrop tiene reintentos y mensaje de error Surfpool.
- ✅ Se ejecutó `anchor build` exitosamente.
- ✅ Se intentó deploy al Surfpool existente sin detenerlo; falló por buffer persistente demasiado pequeño.
- ✅ Se ejecutaron suite/targeted tests con timeout y `--exit`; quedaron bloqueados por Surfpool persistente/429, no por una aserción contractual concluyente.
- ✅ Se guardaron memorias de los fixes y del bloqueo de signer Config.

## Next Steps
- Preguntar una sola aclaración HITL sobre evidencia: confirmar si el producto exige conservar 10 evidencias de hasta 2048 bytes (lo que implica separar en cuentas PDA individuales/equivalente) o si existe un límite funcional menor documentado. No tocar `Dispute` hasta esa respuesta.
- Con el secret del advisor persistente o un reset seguro explícitamente autorizado/posible, rerun build/deploy/suite; el deploy puede requerir resolver el buffer persistente de Surfpool sin matarlo.
- Luego ejecutar Check posterior.

## Relevant Files
- `trust-escrow-v3/programs/trust-escrow-v3/src/lib.rs` — refund de soporte corregido; fixes previos conservados.
- `trust-escrow-v3/tests/escrow.ts` — setup Config idempotente/visible y test de ticket tras milestone.
- `trust-escrow-v3/docs/contract/03-estado.md` — evidencia: tamaño máximo por item, sin decisión explícita de count/arquitectura.
- `trust-escrow-v3/docs/contract/06-disputes.md` — política de soporte y fee.

observations.title: Bloqueo HITL: política de evidencias v3
observations.content:
**What**: La fase Make corrigió reembolso post-milestone y setup idempotente, pero quedó bloqueada al detectar que `Dispute::INIT_SPACE` supera 10.240 bytes con 10 evidencias de 2.048 bytes.
**Why**: La documentación fija 2.048 bytes por evidencia, pero no define si el producto exige conservar 10 ni si las evidencias deben vivir inline o en PDAs separadas. El agente no debe adivinar esta decisión.
**Where**: `trust-escrow-v3/programs/trust-escrow-v3/src/lib.rs` y docs/specs de disputas.
**Learned**: Build pasa; deploy/suite siguen bloqueados por estado persistente de Surfpool (buffer insuficiente/HTTP 429/secret advisor). Se necesita decisión del usuario: conservar 10 x 2.048 en cuentas PDA individuales, o definir un límite menor documentado.

- Surfpool no estaba activo en `127.0.0.1:8899`; se levantó de forma segura como PID 88593 con `surfpool start --manifest-file-path ./txtx.yml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8899 --ws-port 8900 --no-tui -y`.

observations.content:
**What**: El contrato guarda y valida deadlines de job/milestone, pero no los aplica después; tampoco existe auto-aprobación aunque está documentada.

observations.content:
**What**: El runbook despliega el programa pero no ejecuta ni verifica `initialize_config`.
**Why**: Amplifica el P0 de bootstrap permissionless: en una red pública el primer caller puede tomar autoridad.
**Where**: `trust-escrow-v3/runbooks/deployment/main.tx:10-17`, `Anchor.toml`.
**Learned**: El deploy debe bootstrapear Config con authority/advisor/treasuries/fee esperados y verificar valores on-chain y upgrade authority.

observations.title: P2: suite y dependencias no reproducibles
observations.content:
**What**: La auditoría encontró tests insuficientes/bloqueados, endpoint devnet accidental, advisor persistente ausente, Anchor CLI 0.32.1 vs crates 0.30.x, clippy -D warnings fallando y documentación desactualizada respecto a constantes/evidence PDAs/fees.

**Learned**: Forzar localnet en tests, alinear versiones, ampliar negative tests, corregir clippy y sincronizar docs antes de release.

observations.title: P1: ArbiterPool permissionless
observations.content:
**What**: `create_arbiter_pool` permite a cualquier signer crear el PDA global y fijar su propia authority; `assign_arbiter` no liga pool a `Config.authority`.
**Why**: Un atacante puede llenar el pool o bloquear la gobernanza del arbitraje antes de la plataforma.
**Where**: `trust-escrow-v3/programs/trust-escrow-v3/src/lib.rs:779-800, 963-982, 1660-1682`.
**Learned**: La creación/gestión debe exigir `config.authority` o derivar el pool de Config.

observations.title: Fixed screenshot plugin: non-blocking polling, Alt+C cancel, log viewer
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed the screenshot TUI plugin for OpenCode after the user reported it got stuck in "capturing..." state.

**Why**: The original `for/await` polling loop blocked the TUI event loop, preventing the user from interacting with OpenCode. Also, `Alt+X` conflicted with the TTS plugin's stop command.

**Changes made**:
1. Replaced blocking `for/await` loop with non-blocking `setInterval` polling
2. `Alt+C` while capturing now cancels the capture (same key, double-duty)
3. Removed `Alt+X` binding (conflicts with TTS plugin)
4. Added `:screenshot-log` command to view the last 20 lines of the log
5. Clearer toast instructions: "Win+Shift+S → capturar → GUARDAR (Ctrl+S)"
6. Full logging to `/tmp/clipboard/screenshot.log`
7. Clipboard monitoring as primary method, Snips folder as fallback
8. 4 Snips paths checked: default, Pictures, OneDrive/Pictures

**Files**:
- `/home/dcdebian/Proyectos/dcfiles/config/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/screenshot.tsx`
- Symlink: `/home/dcdebian/.config/opencode/tui-plugins/screenshot.tsx`
- Registered in `tui.json`
- Commands in `opencode.json`

**Important**: OpenCode does NOT hot-reload TUI plugins. Must restart OpenCode for changes to take effect.

observations.content:

observations.title: dcfiles add/sync no importa archivos nuevos desde HOME
observations.content:
**What**: Auditoría de dcfiles reveló que `add` y `sync` son unidireccionales (config/ → $HOME). Nunca importan archivos nuevos creados en $HOME dentro de árboles ya gestionados.
**Why**: Usuario agregó plugins nuevos en ~/.config/opencode/plugins y `dcfiles add` no los tomaba.
**Where**: bin/dcfiles (cmd_add:55, cmd_sync:92), lib/symlink.sh (deploy_all:63)
**Learned**:
- `cmd_add` exige `[[ -f "$file" ]]` → rechaza directorios con "File not found". `dcfiles add ~/carpeta` es imposible.
- `cmd_sync` solo llama `deploy_all()` que camina config/ y linkea a $HOME. No existe pasada inversa.
